title: A Phase 1b/2, Randomised, Placebo-controlled Study to Evaluate Safety, Tolerability, Efficacy, and Immunogenicity of VTP-200, a Chimpanzee Adenovirus and Modified Vaccinia Ankara-vectored Multigenotype High-risk Human Papillomavirus Vaccine in Women With Low-grade Cervical Lesions.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The clearance of high-risk oncogenic human papillomaviruses (hrHPV) and related cervical lesions is associated with the development of a robust T-cell response. Therapeutic vaccination that induces HPV antigen-specific T cells is a promising approach. METHOD: A 2-vector dosing strategy using Chimpanzee Adenovirus Oxford 1-HPV and Modified Vaccinia virus Ankara-HPV, both encoding the same multiantigen HPV cassette was given on a 0/28-day schedule to participants with persistent cervical hrHPV and a history of low-grade cervical lesions. An open-label lead-in was followed by a randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled main phase. The primary endpoint was the safety of the different dose regimens; secondary endpoints included immunogenicity, and clearance of hrHPV and associated lesions at 12 months. Nine participants were enrolled in the lead-in and 99 were randomized 67:32 to 5 active dose arms or placebo, respectively. RESULTS: The regimens were well-tolerated with no grade 3-related treatment emergent adverse events or serious adverse reactions. All dosing regimens generated antigen-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell responses. There was no difference in hrHPV clearance between the pooled active groups and placebo (20/64 [31.3%] versus 10/30 [33.3%]; P > .99), nor in lesion clearance. A trend toward higher hrHPV clearance (60%) was observed with the highest Chimpanzee Adenovirus Oxford 1-HPV doses. No association between the peripheral immune response and clearance was demonstrated. CONCLUSIONS: A heterologous, multiantigenic HPV 2-component immunotherapy regimen was well-tolerated and immunogenic but did not result in a statistically significant clearance of either hrHPV or the associated cervical lesions in women with persistent high-risk HPV infections. TRIAL REGISTRATION: EudraCT 2019-001890-98; NCT04607850.

analysis.summary_en: This phase 1b/2 randomized, placebo-controlled study evaluated the safety, tolerability, efficacy, and immunogenicity of VTP-200, a chimpanzee adenovirus and modified vaccinia Ankara-vectored multigenotype high-risk human papillomavirus vaccine in women with low-grade cervical lesions. The study included an open-label lead-in with 9 participants and a main phase with 99 randomized participants (67 active, 32 placebo). The vaccine was well-tolerated with no serious adverse events and induced antigen-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell responses. However, there was no statistically significant difference in hrHPV clearance (31.3% vs 33.3%; P > .99) or lesion clearance between active and placebo groups. The highest dose showed a trend toward higher hrHPV clearance (60%). The authors conclude that while the vaccine is immunogenic, it did not significantly improve hrHPV clearance or lesion resolution in this population.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 开放标签导入期之后是随机、盲法、安慰剂对照的主要阶段。9 名参与者参加了导入试验,99 名参与者以 67:32 的比例分别随机分配到 5 个活性剂量组或安慰剂组。

title: The Association Between Human Papillomavirus and Prostate Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Human papillomavirus (HPV), the necessary cause of cervical cancer, is associated with an increased risk of other anogenital cancers. While HPV has frequently been detected in prostate specimens, its role in prostate carcinogenesis remains controversial. We synthesized and meta‐analyzed the epidemiological literature on the association between HPV and prostate cancer. We completed a systematic search of Embase, MEDLINE, Scopus and Cochrane on January 31, 2025. Two reviewers independently screened articles and extracted data on study design and population, sample characteristics, HPV and prostate cancer ascertainment methods, and results. We pooled risk estimates using a random effects model and performed subgroup meta‐analyses by HPV risk level, genotype, and control group. Our search identified 1874 unique records. Of 84 included articles (1990–2025), 57 were cross‐sectional, 15 case–control, 6 nested case–control, and 6 were cohort studies. HPV detection methods reported were HPV DNA ( n = 57); HPV serology ( n = 17); subjects' self‐report ( n = 5); chart review, registry or claims data ( n = 4); RNA ( n = 3); and immunohistochemistry ( n = 2). Most studies (58.3%) reported HPV prevalence below 20%. Our meta‐analysis (39 studies) produced a pooled odds ratio (OR) of 2.35 (95% CI: 1.87–2.95). When restricted to high‐risk HPV, the pooled OR was 2.75 (95% CI: 1.69–4.46). HPV16, HPV18, and HPV33 had positive associations with prostate cancer (pooled ORs: 2.28, 95% CI: 1.18–4.40; 2.37, 95% CI: 1.16–4.87; 3.73, 95% CI: 0.46–30.30, respectively) and the association was strongest when using normal tissue as controls (pooled OR:4.81, 95% CI: 1.83–12.69). Our findings support a positive association between the detection of oncogenic HPV DNA in prostate specimens and prostate cancer, although its etiologic significance remains unclear.

analysis.methods: The researchers performed a systematic search of Embase, MEDLINE, Scopus, and Cochrane on January 31, 2025, with two independent reviewers screening articles and extracting data; pooled risk estimates were calculated using a random effects model, with subgroup analyses by HPV risk level, genotype, and control group.
analysis.main_results: The meta-analysis of 39 studies yielded a pooled odds ratio (OR) of 2.35 (95% CI: 1.87–2.95) for HPV and prostate cancer, with a higher OR of 2.75 (95% CI: 1.69–4.46) for high-risk HPV; HPV16, HPV18, and HPV33 showed positive associations, and the strongest association was observed when using normal tissue as controls (OR: 4.81, 95% CI: 1.83–12.69).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as supporting a positive association between oncogenic HPV DNA detection in prostate specimens and prostate cancer, though they noted that its etiologic significance remains unclear.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest a potential role for HPV in prostate carcinogenesis, which may inform surveillance strategies and further research into HPV's mechanisms in prostate cancer development.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate, limited by the heterogeneity of study designs, HPV detection methods, and the inability to establish causality; most studies reported HPV prevalence below 20%, and the etiologic significance of HPV in prostate cancer remains uncertain.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized epidemiological evidence on the association between human papillomavirus (HPV) and prostate cancer. The study included 84 articles (1990–2025) and found a pooled odds ratio of 2.35 (95% CI: 1.87–2.95) for HPV and prostate cancer, with a higher association for high-risk HPV (OR: 2.75, 95% CI: 1.69–4.46). HPV16, HPV18, and HPV33 showed positive associations, with the strongest effect when normal tissue was used as controls (OR: 4.81, 95% CI: 1.83–12.69). While the findings support a link between HPV detection and prostate cancer, the etiologic significance remains unclear, and the evidence is limited by study heterogeneity and low HPV prevalence in most samples.

title_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 与前列腺癌之间的关联:系统评价和荟萃分析
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Human papillomavirus (HPV), the necessary cause of cervical cancer, is associated with an increased risk of other anogenital cancers. While HPV has frequently been detected in prostate specimens, its role in prostate carcinogenesis remains controversial. We synthesized and meta‐analyzed the epidemiological literature on the association between HPV and prostate cancer. We completed a systematic search of Embase, MEDLINE, Scopus and Cochrane on January 31, 2025. Two reviewers independently screened articles and extracted data on study design and population, sample characteristics, HPV and prostate cancer ascertainment methods, and results. We pooled risk estimates using a random effects model and performed subgroup meta‐analyses by HPV risk level, genotype, and control group. Our search identified 1874 unique records. Of 84 included articles (1990–2025), 57 were cross‐sectional, 15 case–control, 6 nested case–control, and 6 were cohort studies. HPV detection methods reported were HPV DNA ( n = 57); HPV serology ( n = 17); subjects' self‐report ( n = 5); chart review, registry or claims data ( n = 4); RNA ( n = 3); and immunohistochemistry ( n = 2). Most studies (58.3%) reported HPV prevalence below 20%. Our meta‐analysis (39 studies) produced a pooled odds ratio (OR) of 2.35 (95% CI: 1.87–2.95). When restricted to high‐risk HPV, the pooled OR was 2.75 (95% CI: 1.69–4.46). HPV16, HPV18, and HPV33 had positive associations with prostate cancer (pooled ORs: 2.28, 95% CI: 1.18–4.40; 2.37, 95% CI: 1.16–4.87; 3.73, 95% CI: 0.46–30.30, respectively) and the association was strongest when using normal tissue as controls (pooled OR:4.81, 95% CI: 1.83–12.69). Our findings support a positive association between the detection of oncogenic HPV DNA in prostate specimens and prostate cancer, although its etiologic significance remains unclear.

title: Self-collected versus clinician-collected human papillomavirus samples.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to evaluate the comparability of self-collected and clinician-collected samples for human papillomavirus detection, cytological findings, and identification of infectious agents. METHODS: This prospective controlled clinical trial enrolled 124 women aged 30-65 years due for routine cervical cancer screening. This prospective comparative study enrolled 124 women aged 30-65 years who were eligible for routine cervical cancer screening. Participants were allocated to either a clinician-collected control group (n=51) or a self-collected group (n=73) via systematic allocation based on clinic registration order. Viral deoxyribonucleic acid analysis was performed by multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction; cytological evaluation followed the Bethesda classification system. Infectious agents and participant satisfaction were also assessed. Laboratory personnel were blinded to group allocation. RESULTS: Overall human papillomavirus positivity was 21.8% (27/124), with rates of 27.5% (14/51) in the control group and 17.8% (13/73) in the self-collected group (p=0.200). Cytological abnormalities were detected in 5.5% of self-collected samples (three cases of atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance, one case of atypical squamous cells cannot exclude high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion) versus 0% in the control group (p=0.236). Inflammatory smear findings, Candida (9.8 vs. 8.2%), and Trichomonas vaginalis (0 vs. 1.4%) detection rates were similar between groups. Mean satisfaction score was 12.6±1.62 out of 16 (78.8% positive responses). CONCLUSION: Self-collected human papillomavirus sampling yields results diagnostically comparable to clinician-collected specimens. Self collected human papillomavirus sampling demonstrated similar human papillomavirus detection rates compared with clinician-collected specimens. Given its feasibility and high acceptability, self-collection may serve as an effective complementary approach in cervical cancer screening programs, particularly for reaching women who have not previously participated in screening.

elements_zh.methods: 通过多重实时聚合酶链式反应进行病毒脱氧核糖核酸分析;细胞学评估遵循Bethesda分类系统。还评估了传染源和参与者的满意度。实验室人员对分组分配不知情。

Cytological abnormalities were detected in 5.5% of self-collected samples versus 0% in the control group (p=0.236). Inflammatory smear findings, Candida (9.8 vs. 8.2%), and Trichomonas vaginalis (0 vs. 1.4%) detection rates were similar between groups. Mean satisfaction score was 12.6±1.62 out of 16 (78.8% positive responses).
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 自行采集的 人乳头瘤病毒 采样产生的诊断结果与临床医生采集的标本相当。与临床医生采集的样本相比,自行采集的 人乳头瘤病毒 采样显示出相似的 人乳头瘤病毒 检出率。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 鉴于其可行性和较高的可接受性,自行收集可以作为 宫颈癌 筛查计划的有效补充方法,特别是对于以前未参与筛查的女性。

source_body_en: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to evaluate the comparability of self-collected and clinician-collected samples for human papillomavirus detection, cytological findings, and identification of infectious agents. METHODS: This prospective controlled clinical trial enrolled 124 women aged 30-65 years due for routine cervical cancer screening. This prospective comparative study enrolled 124 women aged 30-65 years who were eligible for routine cervical cancer screening. Participants were allocated to either a clinician-collected control group (n=51) or a self-collected group (n=73) via systematic allocation based on clinic registration order. Viral deoxyribonucleic acid analysis was performed by multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction; cytological evaluation followed the Bethesda classification system. Infectious agents and participant satisfaction were also assessed. Laboratory personnel were blinded to group allocation. RESULTS: Overall human papillomavirus positivity was 21.8% (27/124), with rates of 27.5% (14/51) in the control group and 17.8% (13/73) in the self-collected group (p=0.200). Cytological abnormalities were detected in 5.5% of self-collected samples (three cases of atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance, one case of atypical squamous cells cannot exclude high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion) versus 0% in the control group (p=0.236). Inflammatory smear findings, Candida (9.8 vs. 8.2%), and Trichomonas vaginalis (0 vs. 1.4%) detection rates were similar between groups. Mean satisfaction score was 12.6±1.62 out of 16 (78.8% positive responses). CONCLUSION: Self-collected human papillomavirus sampling yields results diagnostically comparable to clinician-collected specimens. Self collected human papillomavirus sampling demonstrated similar human papillomavirus detection rates compared with clinician-collected specimens. Given its feasibility and high acceptability, self-collection may serve as an effective complementary approach in cervical cancer screening programs, particularly for reaching women who have not previously participated in screening.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估自我收集和临床医生收集的样本在 人乳头瘤病毒 检测、细胞学结果和传染原鉴定方面的可比性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项前瞻性对照临床试验招募了 124 名 30-65 岁的女性,她们有资格接受常规 宫颈癌 筛查。根据诊所登记顺序,通过系统分配,将参与者分配到临床医生收集的对照组(n = 51)或自行收集的组(n = 73)。
analysis_zh.methods: 通过多重实时聚合酶链式反应进行病毒脱氧核糖核酸分析;细胞学评估遵循Bethesda分类系统。还评估了传染源和参与者的满意度。实验室人员对分组分配不知情。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 自行采集的 人乳头瘤病毒 采样产生的诊断结果与临床医生采集的标本相当。与临床医生采集的样本相比,自行采集的 人乳头瘤病毒 采样显示出相似的 人乳头瘤病毒 检出率。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 鉴于其可行性和较高的可接受性,自行收集可以作为 宫颈癌 筛查计划的有效补充方法,特别是对于以前未参与筛查的女性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告研究设计或证据强度评估的具体局限性。

title: The cervicovaginal microbiome: an emerging determinant of HPV infection and disease
abstract: ABSTRACT Human papillomaviruses (HPVs) are epitheliotropic viruses that cause diseases ranging from cutaneous warts to invasive cancers. HPVs exhibit tropism for the epithelial lining of the skin, oral cavity, and anogenital tract. A subset of HPVs, known as high-risk HPVs, have oncogenic potential and cause nearly one-third of all virus-associated cancers worldwide, including essentially all cervical cancers, most other anogenital cancers, and a growing percentage of head and neck cancers. A large and growing body of clinical and epidemiological research has established the host microbiome, or the collection of microorganisms on and within the body, as a key determinant of HPV infection, persistence, and disease development. In this review, an overview of the current understanding of associations between bacterial components of the host cervicovaginal microbiome (CVM) and aspects of HPV pathogenesis is discussed. Potential mechanisms through which the CVM influences HPV infection and neoplastic disease development are also presented. The inherent challenges of studying HPVs and the microbiome have impeded progress to define not only the underlying mechanisms involved in HPV-CVM interactions, but also the ability to address remaining questions such as causality, temporal dynamics, and the directionality of this relationship. Emerging in vitro and in vivo models provide powerful opportunities to address these outstanding questions and increase our understanding of trans-kingdom interactions that contribute to HPV infection and subsequent disease.

title_original: The cervicovaginal microbiome: an emerging determinant of HPV infection and disease

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on human papillomaviruses (HPVs), specifically their role in causing diseases ranging from cutaneous warts to invasive cancers, with emphasis on high-risk HPVs that are oncogenic and associated with cervical, anogenital, and head and neck cancers. The central question examines how the cervicovaginal microbiome (CVM) influences HPV infection, persistence, and disease development.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative overview that synthesizes clinical and epidemiological research on the host microbiome as a determinant of HPV pathogenesis. It does not report specific databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, or study counts, nor does it employ a meta-analysis or consensus process.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: There is strong agreement that the host microbiome, particularly the bacterial components of the cervicovaginal microbiome, is a key determinant of HPV infection, persistence, and disease development. High-risk HPVs are established as the primary cause of nearly one-third of all virus-associated cancers worldwide, including cervical and other anogenital cancers.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Challenges in studying HPVs and the microbiome have hindered progress in defining underlying mechanisms, causality, temporal dynamics, and directionality of HPV-CVM interactions. Evidence gaps remain regarding these unresolved aspects and the specific mechanisms through which the CVM influences HPV pathogenesis.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should focus on addressing outstanding questions through emerging in vitro and in vivo models to better understand trans-kingdom interactions contributing to HPV infection and disease. This includes investigating causality, temporal dynamics, and the directionality of the relationship between the CVM and HPV.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the role of the cervicovaginal microbiome (CVM) as a determinant of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection and disease. High-risk HPVs are established as the cause of nearly one-third of virus-associated cancers, including cervical and other anogenital cancers. While clinical and epidemiological research confirms the CVM's influence on HPV pathogenesis, challenges in studying these interactions have limited progress in defining mechanisms, causality, and temporal dynamics. Emerging models offer opportunities to address these gaps and enhance understanding of trans-kingdom interactions in HPV infection and disease development.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点关注 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV),特别是它们在引起从皮肤疣到侵袭性癌症等疾病中的作用,重点是具有致癌性并与宫颈癌、肛门生殖器癌和头颈癌相关的 高危型HPV。核心问题是检查宫颈阴道微生物组 (CVM) 如何影响 HPV 感染、持续性和疾病发展。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是一篇叙述性概述,综合了 宿主 微生物组作为 HPV 发病机制 决定因素的临床和流行病学研究。它不报告具体的数据库、检索日期、资格标准或研究计数,也不采用荟萃分析或共识过程。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 人们一致认为,宿主 微生物组,特别是宫颈阴道微生物组的细菌成分,是 HPV 感染、持续存在和疾病发展的关键决定因素。高危型HPV 被确定为全世界近三分之一的病毒相关癌症的主要原因,包括宫颈癌和其他肛门生殖器癌。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 研究 HPV 和微生物组的挑战阻碍了定义 HPV-CVM 相互作用的潜在机制、因果关系、时间动态和方向性的进展。关于这些未解决的方面以及 CVM 影响 HPV 发病机制 的具体机制,证据仍然存在差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的研究应侧重于通过新兴的体外和体内模型解决突出问题,以更好地了解导致 HPV 感染和疾病的跨界相互作用。这包括调查 CVM 和 HPV 之间关系的因果关系、时间动态以及方向性。

abstract_zh: 摘要 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 是一种亲上皮病毒,可引起从皮肤疣到侵袭性癌症等多种疾病。HPV 对皮肤、口腔和肛门生殖道的上皮衬里表现出趋向性。HPV 的一个子集(称为 高危型HPV)具有致癌潜力,导致全球近三分之一的病毒相关癌症,包括基本上所有 宫颈癌、大多数其他肛门生殖器癌症以及越来越多的头颈癌。大量且不断增长的临床和流行病学研究已将 宿主 微生物组(即体内和体外的微生物集合)确定为 HPV 感染、持续存在和疾病发展的关键决定因素。在这篇综述中,概述了目前对 宿主 宫颈阴道微生物组 (CVM) 细菌成分与 HPV 发病机制 各方面之间关联的理解。还介绍了 CVM 影响 HPV 感染和肿瘤疾病发展的潜在机制。研究 HPV 和微生物组的固有挑战不仅阻碍了定义 HPV-CVM 相互作用的潜在机制的进展,而且也阻碍了解决诸如因果关系、时间动态和这种关系的方向性等剩余问题的能力。新兴的体外和体内模型为解决这些突出问题提供了强大的机会,并增加我们对导致 HPV 感染和随后疾病的跨界相互作用的理解。

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是一篇叙述性概述,综合了 宿主 微生物组作为 HPV 发病机制 决定因素的临床和流行病学研究。它不报告具体的数据库、检索日期、资格标准或研究计数,也不采用荟萃分析或共识过程。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 人们一致认为,宿主 微生物组,特别是宫颈阴道微生物组的细菌成分,是 HPV 感染、持续存在和疾病发展的关键决定因素。高危型HPV 被确定为全世界近三分之一的病毒相关癌症的主要原因,包括宫颈癌和其他肛门生殖器癌。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 研究 HPV 和微生物组的挑战阻碍了定义 HPV-CVM 相互作用的潜在机制、因果关系、时间动态和方向性的进展。关于这些未解决的方面以及 CVM 影响 HPV 发病机制 的具体机制,证据仍然存在差距。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的研究应侧重于通过新兴的体外和体内模型解决突出问题,以更好地了解导致 HPV 感染和疾病的跨界相互作用。这包括调查 CVM 和 HPV 之间关系的因果关系、时间动态以及方向性。

title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of diagnostic accuracy of urine self-sampling for human papillomavirus detection in cervical cancer screening
abstract: Objective This review assessed the diagnostic accuracy of urine self-sampling for human papillomavirus (HPV) detection compared with clinician-collected cervical and vaginal samples. Methods A systematic search of PubMed, and Embase (January 2013–October 2023) identified full-text English studies evaluating urine-based HPV testing conducted in clinical settings and compared with provider-collected samples. Data were extracted using a standardised form, with sensitivity and specificity as primary outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and QUADAS-C tools. The review followed PRISMA-P guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024511154). A random-effects meta-analysis summarised diagnostic accuracy. Results Of 1657 citations, 13 studies met the inclusion criteria. Urine sampling showed lower sensitivity for detecting high-risk HPV and high-risk HPV-associated high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL) than vaginal samples, although specificities were comparable (87% for urine vs. 88% for vaginal samples). Sensitivity for detecting high-risk HPV-HSIL was 75% for urine, compared with 92% for vaginal and 95% for cervical samples. Cervical samples demonstrated the highest diagnostic accuracy, followed by vaginal samples, while urine samples performed the lowest on the summary receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve. Conclusion Urine self-sampling is a non-invasive and acceptable option but demonstrates reduced sensitivity compared with vaginal and cervical sampling. Despite lower accuracy, its convenience may support screening among women who might otherwise not participate.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述评估了与临床医生在 宫颈癌 筛查项目中收集的宫颈和阴道样本相比,尿液自我取样检测 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染和 HPV 相关的高级鳞状上皮内病变 (HSIL) 的诊断准确性。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这项系统评价遵循 PRISMA-P 指南,在 PROSPERO 中注册 (CRD42024511154),并检索了 PubMed 和 Embase(2013 年 1 月至 2023 年 10 月)的英文全文研究,比较了基于尿液的 HPV 检测与临床环境中提供者收集的样本。使用 QUADAS-2 和 QUADAS-C 工具评估偏倚风险,并通过随机效应荟萃分析总结诊断准确性。

elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述强调,尽管特异性相当,但与阴道和宫颈取样相比,尿液自我取样检测 高危型HPV 和 HPV 相关 HSIL 的敏感性较低。尿液样本的较低诊断性能引起了人们对其筛查可靠性的担忧。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 对于那些可能不会参与的女性来说,尿液自我采样可能是一种非侵入性且可接受的筛查选择,尽管其敏感性较低。需要进一步研究来优化基于尿液的 HPV 检测方案并提高诊断准确性,以匹配或接近阴道和宫颈采样方法的性能。

abstract_zh: 目的 本综述评估了与临床医生采集的宫颈和阴道样本相比,尿液自我取样检测 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 的诊断准确性。方法 对 PubMed 和 Embase(2013 年 1 月至 2023 年 10 月)进行系统检索,确定了全文英文研究,评估了在临床环境中进行的基于尿液的 HPV 检测,并与提供者收集的样本进行了比较。使用标准化表格提取数据,以敏感性和特异性作为主要结果。使用 QUADAS-2 和 QUADAS-C 工具评估偏倚风险。该审查遵循 PRISMA-P 指南并在 PROSPERO 中注册 (CRD42024511154)。随机效应荟萃分析总结了诊断准确性。结果 在 1657 次引用中,13 项研究符合纳入标准。尿液取样检测 高危型HPV 和 高危型HPV 相关的高级鳞状上皮内病变 (HSIL) 的敏感性低于阴道样本,但特异性相当(尿液样本为 87%,阴道样本为 88%)。尿液中 高危型HPV-HSIL 的检测灵敏度为 75%,而阴道样本和宫颈样本的灵敏度分别为 92% 和 95%。宫颈样本的诊断准确性最高,其次是阴道样本,而尿液样本在总体受试者工作特征 (ROC) 曲线上的表现最低。结论 尿液自我取样是一种无创且可接受的选择,但与阴道和宫颈取样相比,其敏感性较低。尽管准确性较低,但其便利性可能有助于对原本可能不会参与的女性进行筛查。

analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述强调,尽管特异性相当,但与阴道和宫颈取样相比,尿液自我取样检测 高危型HPV 和 HPV 相关 HSIL 的敏感性较低。尿液样本的较低诊断性能引起了人们对其筛查可靠性的担忧。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 对于那些可能不会参与的女性来说,尿液自我采样可能是一种非侵入性且可接受的筛查选择,尽管其敏感性较低。需要进一步研究来优化基于尿液的 HPV 检测方案并提高诊断准确性,以匹配或接近阴道和宫颈采样方法的性能。

title: Behavioral profiles associated with anal HPV infection among MSM attending university in China: a latent class analysis
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a prevalent sexually transmitted infection (STI) among men who have sex with men (MSM) attending university. Our study aimed to identify distinct behavioral profiles for anal HPV infection in this population using Latent Class Analysis (LCA) and assess factors associated with high-risk behavior. METHODS: We recruited MSM attending university in the University Student HIV Test Intervention Study (UniTest Study) between January and April 2019 in China. Participants completed a self-administered online questionnaire on socio-demographic and sexual behavior characteristics. Participants self-collected anal swabs for HPV genotyping. LCA classified individuals into high and low-risk groups for anal HPV infection based on sexual and related risk behaviors. RESULTS: LCA identified two distinct groups among 292 MSM attending university. The class 2 group exhibited a significantly elevated anal HPV infection rate (52.90%, P < 0.001) compared to the class 1 group (25.55%). Notably, the class 2 group was characterized by higher engagement in casual sex (74.15% vs. 42.87%), having non-student sex partners (77.24% vs. 38.22%), involvement in drunken sex in the past year (26.40% vs. 10.90%), Novel Psychoactive Substances (NPS) use sex history (53.13% vs. 12.88%), and a higher prevalence of HIV testing history (98.80% vs. These findings indicate that the higher-risk behavioral profile was associated with a higher observed prevalence of anal HPV infection. CONCLUSION: Our study identified distinct behavioral profiles associated with anal HPV infection among MSM attending university in China. Tailored interventions addressing substance use (alcohol and NPS), sexual health education emphasizing consistent condom use, and the promotion of HPV vaccination within student health programs are warranted. On-campus HPV testing services represent a potentially valuable service model, but their feasibility, acceptability, and integration into existing health infrastructure require further evaluation before routine implementation. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, www.chictr.org.cn : ChiCTR1900020645. Date of Registration: 2019.09.11.

title: Perceived facilitators and barriers against human papillomavirus vaccine among rural parents with eligible daughters in the Alle district, Southern Ethiopia
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Human papillomavirus vaccine acceptance is influenced by the parental perceptions of the vaccine, but there are few related studies in Ethiopia, and most have focused on quantitative approaches. Therefore, this qualitative study intended to explore parental perceptions about the human papillomavirus vaccine acceptance. OBJECTIVE: To explore the perceived facilitators and barriers against human papillomavirus among rural parents with eligible daughters in the Alle district, southern Ethiopia. METHODS: A qualitative study using focus group discussion and in-depth interviews was conducted from April 25, 2023, to May 25, 2023, among eligible parents of daughters in the Alle district, southern Ethiopia. A convenience sample of 53 parents was recruited for focus group discussions, and 15 parents were purposely sampled for in-depth interviews. The data were collected by a semi-structured focus group discussion guide and in-depth interview questionnaires. The interview data were translated into English after transcription, and thematic analysis was done by Atlas software version 7.1.16. RESULTS: Among the total participants, 66.2% were female parents and 60.2% were protestant religious followers. Findings were split between two major themes: perceived facilitators and barriers to human papillomavirus vaccine acceptance. The perceived facilitators identified were preventing cervical cancer, seeing it as an expression of parental role and responsibility, and believing in the recommendation of health professionals as facilitators of human papillomavirus vaccination. The identified perceived barriers to human papillomavirus vaccination included: a lack of awareness, a lack of reliable information sources, a lack of trust in the vaccine, misconceptions, fear of side effects, and cultural and religious factors affecting the acceptance of human papillomavirus vaccination. CONCLUSION: Parents identified various facilitators and barriers to accepting the human papillomavirus vaccine. Therefore, we recommend that the government and concerned institutions work in collaboration to address the identified challenges to improve the acceptance of human papillomavirus vaccination.

title_zh: 埃塞俄比亚南部阿勒地区有符合资格女儿的农村父母对 人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗 的感知促进因素和障碍
source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: Human papillomavirus vaccine acceptance is influenced by the parental perceptions of the vaccine, but there are few related studies in Ethiopia, and most have focused on quantitative approaches. Therefore, this qualitative study intended to explore parental perceptions about the human papillomavirus vaccine acceptance. OBJECTIVE: To explore the perceived facilitators and barriers against human papillomavirus among rural parents with eligible daughters in the Alle district, southern Ethiopia. METHODS: A qualitative study using focus group discussion and in-depth interviews was conducted from April 25, 2023, to May 25, 2023, among eligible parents of daughters in the Alle district, southern Ethiopia. A convenience sample of 53 parents was recruited for focus group discussions, and 15 parents were purposely sampled for in-depth interviews. The data were collected by a semi-structured focus group discussion guide and in-depth interview questionnaires. The interview data were translated into English after transcription, and thematic analysis was done by Atlas software version 7.1.16. RESULTS: Among the total participants, 66.2% were female parents and 60.2% were protestant religious followers. Findings were split between two major themes: perceived facilitators and barriers to human papillomavirus vaccine acceptance. The perceived facilitators identified were preventing cervical cancer, seeing it as an expression of parental role and responsibility, and believing in the recommendation of health professionals as facilitators of human papillomavirus vaccination. The identified perceived barriers to human papillomavirus vaccination included: a lack of awareness, a lack of reliable information sources, a lack of trust in the vaccine, misconceptions, fear of side effects, and cultural and religious factors affecting the acceptance of human papillomavirus vaccination. CONCLUSION: Parents identified various facilitators and barriers to accepting the human papillomavirus vaccine. Therefore, we recommend that the government and concerned institutions work in collaboration to address the identified challenges to improve the acceptance of human papillomavirus vaccination.
abstract_zh: 简介:人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗 的接受程度受到家长对 疫苗 认知的影响,但埃塞俄比亚的相关研究很少,大多数都集中在定量方法上。因此,本定性研究旨在探讨家长对 人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗 接受的看法。目的:探讨埃塞俄比亚南部阿勒地区有符合条件的女儿的农村父母对 人乳头瘤病毒 的感知促进因素和障碍。方法:2023 年 4 月 25 日至 2023 年 5 月 25 日,对埃塞俄比亚南部阿勒地区符合条件的女儿家长进行了一项定性研究,采用焦点小组讨论和深入访谈的方式进行。我们随机抽取了 53 名家长进行焦点小组讨论,并特意抽取了 15 名家长进行深度访谈。数据通过半结构化焦点小组讨论指南和深度访谈问卷收集。访谈资料转录后翻译成英文,并通过Atlas软件7.1.16版进行主题分析。结果:在所有参与者中,66.2%是女性父母,60.2%是新教信徒。调查结果分为两个主要主题:人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗 接受的感知促进因素和障碍。所确定的感知促进者正在阻止 宫颈癌,将其视为父母角色和责任的表达,并相信卫生专业人员作为 人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗接种 促进者的建议。已确定的 人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗接种 感知障碍包括:缺乏认识、缺乏可靠的信息来源、对 疫苗 缺乏信任、误解、对副作用的恐惧以及影响 人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗接种 接受的文化和宗教因素。结论:家长确定了接受 人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗 的各种促进因素和障碍。因此,我们建议政府和相关机构合作解决已发现的挑战,以提高 人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗接种 的接受度。

title: Type-specific sensitivity versus detection breadth in HPV diagnostics: improved analytical detection of HPV16/18 by nested PCR
abstract: Abstract Accurate detection of high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) is central to cervical cancer screening. Current diagnostic strategies increasingly prioritize broad-spectrum assays to maximize genotype coverage. However, theoretical genotype breadth does not necessarily translate into effective sample-level detection when clinically dominant targets are present at low copy number. Here, we evaluated this analytical trade-off using conventional PCR as a controlled experimental framework. Type-specific nested PCR assays targeting HPV16 and HPV18 were developed and applied to 41 cervical samples. Nested PCR showed markedly higher relative analytical sensitivity than single-round amplification and produced a greater proportion of specific and interpretable detections than the broad-spectrum consensus systems tested here (MY09/11 and GP5/6). HPV16 and/or HPV18 DNA was detected by nested PCR in 22/41 samples, whereas MY09/11 and GP5/6 detected 11/41 and 2/41 samples, respectively, under the tested conditions. These findings indicate that broad genotype coverage and effective detection of positive samples are distinct analytical properties. In settings where prevalent HPV targets occur at low abundance, a highly sensitive genotype-focused assay may reveal more target-positive samples than a broader but less sensitive consensus approach. The results are not intended to replace clinically validated broad-spectrum screening assays, but they support explicit preservation of per-target analytical sensitivity in reflex testing and future multi-target HPV assay design.
authors: Beatriz Helena Dantas Rodrigues De Albuquerque
Maryana Thalyta Ferreira Câmara De Oliveira

However, theoretical genotype breadth does not necessarily translate into effective sample-level detection when clinically dominant targets are present at low copy number. Here, we evaluated this analytical trade-off using conventional PCR as a controlled experimental framework. Type-specific nested PCR assays targeting HPV16 and HPV18 were developed and applied to 41 cervical samples. Nested PCR showed markedly higher relative analytical sensitivity than single-round amplification and produced a greater proportion of specific and interpretable detections than the broad-spectrum consensus systems tested here (MY09/11 and GP5/6). HPV16 and/or HPV18 DNA was detected by nested PCR in 22/41 samples, whereas MY09/11 and GP5/6 detected 11/41 and 2/41 samples, respectively, under the tested conditions. These findings indicate that broad genotype coverage and effective detection of positive samples are distinct analytical properties. In settings where prevalent HPV targets occur at low abundance, a highly sensitive genotype-focused assay may reveal more target-positive samples than a broader but less sensitive consensus approach. The results are not intended to replace clinically validated broad-spectrum screening assays, but they support explicit preservation of per-target analytical sensitivity in reflex testing and future multi-target HPV assay design.

abstract_zh: 摘要 准确检测高危型 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 是 宫颈癌 筛查的核心。当前的诊断策略越来越优先考虑广谱检测,以最大限度地提高基因型覆盖率。然而,当临床显性靶标以低拷贝数存在时,理论基因型宽度不一定转化为有效的样本水平检测。在这里,我们使用传统 PCR 作为受控实验框架来评估这种分析权衡。针对 HPV16 和 HPV18 的类型特异性巢式 PCR 检测已开发出来并应用于 41 个宫颈样本。巢式 PCR 显示出比单轮扩增明显更高的相对分析灵敏度,并且比此处测试的广谱共识系统(MY09/11 和 GP5/6)产生更大比例的特异性和可解释的检测。在测试条件下,通过巢式PCR在22/41个样本中检测到HPV16和/或HPV18 DNA,而MY09/11和GP5/6分别检测到11/41和2/41个样本。这些发现表明广泛的基因型覆盖和阳性样本的有效检测是独特的分析特性。在普遍 HPV 靶标丰度较低的情况下,与更广泛但敏感性较低的共识方法相比,高度敏感的基因型重点检测可能会揭示更多的靶标阳性样本。这些结果并非旨在取代经过临床验证的广谱筛查测定,但它们支持在反射测试和未来的多目标 HPV 测定设计中明确保留每个目标的分析灵敏度。

title: Occupational human papillomavirus exposure risks for laryngeal surgeons and phoniatricians: A joint European Laryngological Society (ELS) and Union of European Phoniatricians (UEP) Delphi clinical consensus statement
abstract: Abstract Purpose Laser surgical management of human papillomavirus (HPV)-related disease, such as recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP), in the upper aerodigestive tract generates surgical smoke, which may represent a source of occupational viral exposure for laryngeal surgeons, phoniatricians, anesthesia providers and scrub nurses. Despite growing awareness, protective measures remain inconsistently implemented. This study aimed to develop an evidence-informed clinical consensus statement (CCS) to guide occupational HPV risk management in laryngology. Methods A modified Delphi consensus process was conducted under the auspices of the European Laryngological Society (ELS) and the Union of the European Phoniatricians (UEP). A panel of 26 international experts undertook three rounds of voting on 18 statements across five domains: definitions and risk perception, personal protective measures, smoke evacuation and ventilation, preventive vaccination, and areas for further research. Results All panellists completed all three rounds. Of the 18 statements, one reached strong consensus, seven reached consensus, one reached near consensus and six did not reach consensus. Three statements were merged across rounds. Key areas of consensus included the recognition of surgical smoke as a potential occupational HPV exposure risk, the inadequacy of standard surgical masks, the importance of offering HPV vaccination to healthcare workers with potential occupational exposure, alongside areas for further research. Conclusion This joint ELS and UEP CCS represents the first internationally coordinated effort to address occupational HPV exposure in laryngology. While consensus was reached in several key areas, the findings underscore the need for targeted research and greater consistency in protective measures, educational provision and regulatory frameworks.

title_zh: 喉外科医生和听力医师的职业 人乳头瘤病毒 暴露风险:欧洲喉科协会 (ELS) 和欧洲听力医师联盟 (UEP) 德尔菲联合临床共识声明
source_body_en: Abstract Purpose Laser surgical management of human papillomavirus (HPV)-related disease, such as recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP), in the upper aerodigestive tract generates surgical smoke, which may represent a source of occupational viral exposure for laryngeal surgeons, phoniatricians, anesthesia providers and scrub nurses. Despite growing awareness, protective measures remain inconsistently implemented. This study aimed to develop an evidence-informed clinical consensus statement (CCS) to guide occupational HPV risk management in laryngology. Methods A modified Delphi consensus process was conducted under the auspices of the European Laryngological Society (ELS) and the Union of the European Phoniatricians (UEP). A panel of 26 international experts undertook three rounds of voting on 18 statements across five domains: definitions and risk perception, personal protective measures, smoke evacuation and ventilation, preventive vaccination, and areas for further research. Results All panellists completed all three rounds. Of the 18 statements, one reached strong consensus, seven reached consensus, one reached near consensus and six did not reach consensus. Three statements were merged across rounds. Key areas of consensus included the recognition of surgical smoke as a potential occupational HPV exposure risk, the inadequacy of standard surgical masks, the importance of offering HPV vaccination to healthcare workers with potential occupational exposure, alongside areas for further research. Conclusion This joint ELS and UEP CCS represents the first internationally coordinated effort to address occupational HPV exposure in laryngology. While consensus was reached in several key areas, the findings underscore the need for targeted research and greater consistency in protective measures, educational provision and regulatory frameworks.
abstract_zh: 摘要 目的 对上呼吸消化道中的 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 相关疾病(如复发性呼吸道乳头状瘤病 (RRP))进行激光手术治疗时会产生手术烟雾,这可能是喉外科医生、语音科医生、麻醉人员和护士的职业病毒暴露来源。尽管人们的认识不断提高,但保护措施的实施仍然不一致。本研究旨在制定一份循证临床共识声明 (CCS),以指导喉科职业 HPV 风险管理。方法 在欧洲喉科协会 (ELS) 和欧洲语音医师联盟 (UEP) 的支持下进行了修改后的德尔菲共识流程。由 26 名国际专家组成的小组对 18 项声明进行了三轮投票,涉及五个领域:定义和风险认知、个人防护措施、排烟和通风、预防性 疫苗接种 以及进一步研究领域。结果 所有小组成员都完成了全部三轮。18份声明中,1份达成强烈共识,7份达成共识,1份达成接近共识,6份未达成共识。各轮中合并了三份声明。达成共识的关键领域包括认识到手术烟雾是潜在的职业 HPV 暴露风险、标准手术口罩的不足、向可能职业暴露的医护人员提供 HPV 疫苗接种 的重要性,以及需要进一步研究的领域。结论 ELS 和 UEP CCS 联合代表了第一个国际协调行动,旨在解决喉科职业 HPV 暴露问题。虽然在几个关键领域达成了共识,但研究结果强调需要进行有针对性的研究,并在保护措施、教育提供和监管框架方面提高一致性。

title: Association of vaginal dysbiosis with cervical lesions among women with non-16/18 high-risk HPV infections: a cross-sectional study of 2,264 women in Eastern China
abstract: BACKGROUND: To investigate whether vaginal dysbiosis is associated with an increased risk of cervical lesions infected with non-16/18 high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) genotypes and to inform risk-stratified cervical cancer screening strategies. METHODS: This cross‐sectional study included 2,264 women attending Jiaxing Maternal and Child Health Hospital between June 2023 and October 2024. HPV genotyping, vaginal microecological assessment, and Thinprep cytologic test (TCT) were performed. HR- HR-HPV infections were classified as HPV16/18-positive or non-16/18 HR-HPV infections. Logistic regression models were used to evaluate associations, adjusting for age. Multiplicative interaction was assessed using Wald tests for product terms. Benjamini‐Hochberg FDR correction was applied for multiple comparisons. RESULTS: The overall HPV prevalence was 49.87%, with HR-HPV detected in 36.13%. HR‐HPV infection was significantly associated with cervical lesions in both normal (OR = 11.45) and dysbiotic (OR = 4.40) vaginal microbiota (both P < 0.001). Stratified analyses showed higher point estimates for HPV58 and HPV59 in the dysbiosis group (OR = 10.98 and 9.51, respectively) than in the normal group (OR = 7.50 and 6.44, respectively). However, formal multiplicative interaction tests did not reach statistical significance (Wald P = 0.526 and 0.559, respectively; FDR‐adjusted q = 0.559 for both). No HPV subtype remained significantly associated with ASC‐US after FDR correction. CONCLUSIONS: In this cross‐sectional study, vaginal dysbiosis is specifically associated with cervical lesions among women with non‐16/18 HR‐HPV infections, particularly HPV58 and HPV59, which showed elevated point estimates in the presence of dysbiosis. However, formal multiplicative interaction tests did not reach statistical significance. These findings are exploratory and hypothesis‐generating; causality cannot be inferred due to the cross‐sectional design. Prospective studies are needed to validate the observed associations before any clinical application can be considered. Our results should be interpreted with caution and do not support changes to current screening practice.

title_zh: 非 16/18 高危型HPV 感染女性阴道生态失调与宫颈病变的关联:一项针对中国东部地区 2,264 名女性的横断面研究
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: To investigate whether vaginal dysbiosis is associated with an increased risk of cervical lesions infected with non-16/18 high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) genotypes and to inform risk-stratified cervical cancer screening strategies. METHODS: This cross‐sectional study included 2,264 women attending Jiaxing Maternal and Child Health Hospital between June 2023 and October 2024. HPV genotyping, vaginal microecological assessment, and Thinprep cytologic test (TCT) were performed. HR- HR-HPV infections were classified as HPV16/18-positive or non-16/18 HR-HPV infections. Logistic regression models were used to evaluate associations, adjusting for age. Multiplicative interaction was assessed using Wald tests for product terms. Benjamini‐Hochberg FDR correction was applied for multiple comparisons. RESULTS: The overall HPV prevalence was 49.87%, with HR-HPV detected in 36.13%. HR‐HPV infection was significantly associated with cervical lesions in both normal (OR = 11.45) and dysbiotic (OR = 4.40) vaginal microbiota (both P < 0.001). Stratified analyses showed higher point estimates for HPV58 and HPV59 in the dysbiosis group (OR = 10.98 and 9.51, respectively) than in the normal group (OR = 7.50 and 6.44, respectively). However, formal multiplicative interaction tests did not reach statistical significance (Wald P = 0.526 and 0.559, respectively; FDR‐adjusted q = 0.559 for both). No HPV subtype remained significantly associated with ASC‐US after FDR correction. CONCLUSIONS: In this cross‐sectional study, vaginal dysbiosis is specifically associated with cervical lesions among women with non‐16/18 HR‐HPV infections, particularly HPV58 and HPV59, which showed elevated point estimates in the presence of dysbiosis. However, formal multiplicative interaction tests did not reach statistical significance. These findings are exploratory and hypothesis‐generating; causality cannot be inferred due to the cross‐sectional design. Prospective studies are needed to validate the observed associations before any clinical application can be considered. Our results should be interpreted with caution and do not support changes to current screening practice.

title: Effects of a Message‐Framing Video Intervention on Maternal Vaccine Confidence Regarding HPV Vaccination for Daughters: A Quasi‐Experimental Study Among Mothers With Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Increasing HPV vaccination coverage is pivotal, necessitating effective vaccination strategies. This research assessed the impact of a message‐framing (MF) video intervention on boosting vaccine confidence among mothers diagnosed with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN), targeting HPV vaccination for their daughters. Methods Conducted from January to June 2024, this interventional study took place at the gynecological cervical clinic of a university‐affiliated hospital and targeted CIN patients from adjacent communities. Mothers with daughters aged 9–14 years, who were unvaccinated and whose mothers were diagnosed with CIN, participated. They were allocated to receive either standard health education or a targeted message‐framing video intervention. Outcome data were collected by trained researchers after a 10‐week intervention period, focusing on maternal knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors toward their daughters’ HPV vaccination. Results A total of 101 patients were analyzed. Those exposed to the message‐framing video intervention exhibited significantly improved knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors towards HPV vaccination ( Z = −3.376, P = 0.001), and demonstrated lower vaccine hesitancy scores ( Z = −2.924, P = 0.003) compared to their counterparts receiving standard health education. However, differences in the rates of scheduling vaccine appointments were not statistically significant between the groups ( χ 2 = 0.934, P = 0.334). Conclusions The message‐framing video intervention significantly enhanced vaccine confidence by improving the knowledge and willingness of CIN patients to vaccinate their daughters against HPV. Further studies are required to explore the intervention's influence on actual vaccination rates.

title: Nonavalent HPV vaccination induces robust systemic and mucosal HPV16-neutralizing antibody responses in previously infected women
abstract: Abstract Background Neutralizing antibody responses to human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines are typically assessed in serum, while mucosal immunity at sites of infection remains less well characterized, particularly in HPV-positive individuals. We evaluated systemic and mucosal HPV16-neutralizing antibody responses following nonavalent HPV vaccination in women with a recent HPV16/18-positive cervical test. Methods In this longitudinal RIFT-HPV study, 39 previously unvaccinated adult women with an HPV16/18-positive cervical test done in the previous 12 months received a three-dose schedule of the nonavalent HPV vaccine (Gardasil-9). Paired serum, cervical, and oral samples were collected before and during vaccination. Neutralizing activity against HPV16 pseudovirions was measured using an enhanced green fluorescent protein pseudovirion-based neutralization assay (EGFP-PBNA). Results Vaccination significantly increased HPV16-neutralizing antibody responses in serum, cervical, and oral samples, irrespective of baseline HPV16 positivity. Serum EC 50 detection increased from 33% at baseline to 100% after three doses, while cervical and oral detection increased from 8% and 10% after one dose, to 100% and 80% after three doses, respectively. With assay conditions exceeding physiological viral exposure levels, cervical HPV16 pseudovirion neutralization progressively increased from 36% before vaccination to 61%, 68% and 78% after one, two and three vaccine doses, respectively. Systemic and mucosal neutralizing responses were positively correlated. The EGFP-PBNA demonstrated high reproducibility (ICC = 0.98) and good concordance with the reference method. Conclusions Nonavalent HPV vaccination induced strong systemic and mucosal HPV16-neutralizing antibody responses, regardless of current HPV16 positivity. These findings demonstrate enhanced mucosal HPV16-neutralizing immunity following nonavalent vaccination in previously infected women and support further investigation of its potential role in reducing viral infectivity and transmission. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05334706. Registered on 19 April 2022.

abstract_zh: 摘要背景 对 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗 的中和抗体反应通常在血清中进行评估,而感染部位的粘膜免疫仍然不太清楚,特别是在 HPV 阳性个体中。我们评估了近期 HPV16/18 宫颈检测呈阳性的女性在感染非价 HPV 疫苗接种 后的全身和粘膜 HPV16 中和抗体反应。方法 在这项纵向 RIFT-HPV 研究中,39 名之前未接种疫苗且在过去 12 个月内进行过 HPV16/18 宫颈检测呈阳性的成年女性接受了非价 HPV 疫苗 (Gardasil-9) 的三剂方案。在 疫苗接种 之前和期间收集配对血清、宫颈和口腔样本。使用增强型绿色荧光蛋白假病毒粒子中和测定 (EGFP-PBNA) 测量针对 HPV16 假病毒粒子的中和活性。结果 疫苗接种 显着增加血清、宫颈和口腔样本中 HPV16 中和抗体反应,无论基线 HPV16 阳性如何。血清 EC 50 检测从基线时的 33% 增加到三剂后的 100%,而宫颈和口腔检测分别从一剂后的 8% 和 10% 增加到三剂后的 100% 和 80%。当检测条件超过生理病毒暴露水平时,宫颈HPV16假病毒粒子中和度从疫苗接种前的36%逐渐增加到疫苗一剂、两剂和三剂后的61%、68%和78%,分别。全身和粘膜中和反应呈正相关。EGFP-PBNA 表现出高重现性 (ICC = 0.98),并且与参考方法具有良好的一致性。结论 无论当前 HPV16 阳性如何,非价 HPV 疫苗接种 都会诱导强烈的全身和粘膜 HPV16 中和抗体反应。这些发现表明,在先前感染的女性中,非价 传播 后粘膜 HPV16 中和免疫力增强,并支持进一步研究其在降低病毒感染性和 传播 方面的潜在作用。试验注册:ClinicalTrials.gov,NCT05334706。注册日期:2022 年 4 月 19 日。

title: Trends in incidence and medical costs of human papillomavirus–related diseases in Korea: evidence from National Health Insurance claims
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is a major cause of cervical, anal and oropharyngeal cancers. Although Korea has implemented a national HPV vaccination programme since 2016, nationwide evidence on incidence trends and medical costs of HPV-related diseases remains limited. METHODS: This retrospective population-based study analysed Korean National Health Insurance Service claims data. Age-standardised incidence (ASI) rates of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN1 and CIN2/3), genital warts (GWs), and cervical, oropharyngeal and anal cancers from 2015 to 2022 were calculated using the 2022 Korean population as the standard. Trends in ASI were analysed using Joinpoint regression with a piecewise log-linear (Poisson) model. For diseases with and without statistically significant Joinpoints, trends were reported using pre-identified and post-identified segment-specific annual percentage changes (APCs) and the average annual percentage change (AAPC), respectively. Trends in total medical costs from 2015 to 2021 were evaluated using linear regression. RESULTS: ASI trends differed by sex and disease type. Cervical cancer incidence among females declined significantly during 2015-2022 (AAPC; -4.2%, p<0.001). Joinpoint regression identified significant inflection points in 2019 for both female and male GWs. Female GW incidence increased during 2015-2019 (APC; 3.7%, p=0.010) and then decreased significantly during 2019-2022 (APC; -14.0%, p<0.001). Male GW incidence increased significantly during 2015-2019 (APC; 11.3%, p<0.001) and then showed no statistically significant change during 2019-2022 (APC; 1.4%, p=0.290). CONCLUSIONS: These descriptive findings provide population-level evidence on HPV-associated disease burden in Korea but cannot establish causal attribution to vaccination, screening or other preventive interventions, necessitating continued surveillance with individual-level data linkage.

title: Prevalence, genotype distribution, and viral load characteristics of high-risk HPV infection among 42,379 women in Beijing, China: a retrospective study
abstract: Abstract Background Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection is a necessary cause of cervical cancer, while its prevalence and genotype distribution show substantial regional variation. This study aimed to characterize HR-HPV infection among women in Beijing and provide region-specific epidemiological evidence for local prevention strategies. Methods This retrospective analysis included 42,379 women who underwent cervical HPV genotyping at Dongzhimen Hospital, Beijing University of Chinese Medicine, from March 2016 to December 2024. Fifteen HR-HPV genotypes were detected using fluorescent PCR. Age-specific infection patterns were assessed across seven age groups, and viral load was categorized into three levels. The study period was divided into three phases based on the temporal progression of the COVID-19 outbreak: pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic. Results The overall HR-HPV prevalence was 19.91% (8,438/42,379). HPV52 (20.17%), HPV58 (12.61%), and HPV16 (11.84%) were the most common genotypes. Single-type infections predominated (75.09%), while multiple-type infections accounted for 24.91%, with HPV52 + HPV58, HPV52 + HPV16, and HPV52 + HPV51 being the most frequent combinations. Age distribution showed a bimodal pattern, with peaks at 20–29 years (38.53%) and 60–69 years (29.55%). Moderate viral load was most common (40.08%); HPV31 and HPV16 had the highest proportions of high viral loads, while HPV52 displayed a "high prevalence–low viral load" pattern. High viral load proportion increased with infection complexity. Annual prevalence ranged from 17.9% to 22.0%, with the lowest rate in 2020. Across pandemic phases, overall prevalence was 20.53%, 19.40%, and 19.88%, while multiple-type infection rates declined consecutively from 27.39% to 21.65%. Conclusions HR-HPV infection in Beijing women is characterized by predominance of HPV52, HPV58, and HPV16, a bimodal age distribution, and genotype-specific viral load profiles. The pandemic-associated decline in overall prevalence and sustained decrease in multiple-type infections underscore the importance of targeted vaccination and screening strategies in the post-pandemic era.

This study aimed to characterize HR-HPV infection among women in Beijing and provide region-specific epidemiological evidence for local prevention strategies. Methods This retrospective analysis included 42,379 women who underwent cervical HPV genotyping at Dongzhimen Hospital, Beijing University of Chinese Medicine, from March 2016 to December 2024. Fifteen HR-HPV genotypes were detected using fluorescent PCR. Age-specific infection patterns were assessed across seven age groups, and viral load was categorized into three levels. The study period was divided into three phases based on the temporal progression of the COVID-19 outbreak: pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic. Results The overall HR-HPV prevalence was 19.91% (8,438/42,379). HPV52 (20.17%), HPV58 (12.61%), and HPV16 (11.84%) were the most common genotypes. Single-type infections predominated (75.09%), while multiple-type infections accounted for 24.91%, with HPV52 + HPV58, HPV52 + HPV16, and HPV52 + HPV51 being the most frequent combinations. Age distribution showed a bimodal pattern, with peaks at 20–29 years (38.53%) and 60–69 years (29.55%). Moderate viral load was most common (40.08%); HPV31 and HPV16 had the highest proportions of high viral loads, while HPV52 displayed a "high prevalence–low viral load" pattern. High viral load proportion increased with infection complexity. Annual prevalence ranged from 17.9% to 22.0%, with the lowest rate in 2020. Across pandemic phases, overall prevalence was 20.53%, 19.40%, and 19.88%, while multiple-type infection rates declined consecutively from 27.39% to 21.65%. Conclusions HR-HPV infection in Beijing women is characterized by predominance of HPV52, HPV58, and HPV16, a bimodal age distribution, and genotype-specific viral load profiles. The pandemic-associated decline in overall prevalence and sustained decrease in multiple-type infections underscore the importance of targeted vaccination and screening strategies in the post-pandemic era.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the prevalence, genotype distribution, and viral load characteristics of high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection among 42,379 women in Beijing, China, from 2016 to 2024. Using fluorescent PCR, the researchers identified the most common HR-HPV genotypes as HPV52, HPV58, and HPV16, with single-type infections predominating. The study found a bimodal age distribution pattern, with peaks in the 20–29 and 60–69 age groups. It also noted a decline in overall prevalence and multiple-type infections during the pandemic period. These findings highlight the need for targeted vaccination and screening strategies in Beijing. However, the study's retrospective design and single-center data collection may limit its generalizability, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 持续高危型人乳头瘤病毒(HR-HPV)感染是导致宫颈癌的必要原因,而其患病率和基因型分布则表现出显着的地区差异。本研究旨在了解北京地区女性HR-HPV感染特征,为当地预防策略提供特定区域的流行病学证据。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性分析包括 2016 年 3 月至 2024 年 12 月在北京中医药大学东直门医院接受宫颈 HPV 基因分型的 42,379 名女性。研究期间根据 COVID-19 暴发 的时间进展分为三个阶段:大流行前、大流行和大流行后。
elements_zh.methods: 使用荧光 PCR 检测到 15 种 HR-HPV 基因型。对七个年龄组的特定年龄感染模式进行了评估,并将病毒载量分为三个级别。
elements_zh.main_results: 总体 HR-HPV 患病率 为 19.91% (8,438/42,379)。HPV52(20.17%)、HPV58(12.61%)和HPV16(11.84%)是最常见的基因型。以单型感染为主(75.09%),多型感染占24.91%,其中以HPV52+HPV58、HPV52+HPV16、HPV52+HPV51最为常见。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 与大流行相关的总体 患病率 下降和多种类型感染的持续下降强调了大流行后时代有针对性的 疫苗接种 和筛查策略的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为北京 HR-HPV 感染的 流行病学 提供了重要的见解,可以为制定特定区域的预防和控制策略提供参考。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是回顾性的,基于一家医院的数据,这可能会限制普遍性。由于该研究的观察性质,证据的强度中等。

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景持续高危型人乳头瘤病毒(HR-HPV)感染是导致宫颈癌的必要原因,其患病率和基因型分布存在较大的地区差异。本研究旨在了解北京地区女性HR-HPV感染特征,为当地预防策略提供特定区域的流行病学证据。方法回顾性分析2016年3月至2024年12月在北京中医药大学东直门医院接受宫颈HPV基因分型的42,379例女性,采用荧光PCR技术检测出15种HR-HPV基因型。对七个年龄组的特定年龄感染模式进行了评估,并将病毒载量分为三个级别。根据 COVID-19 暴发 的时间进展,研究期分为三个阶段:大流行前、大流行和大流行后。结果 HR-HPV 患病率 总体率为 19.91% (8,438/42,379)。HPV52(20.17%)、HPV58(12.61%)和HPV16(11.84%)是最常见的基因型。以单型感染为主(75.09%),多型感染占24.91%,其中以HPV52+HPV58、HPV52+HPV16、HPV52+HPV51最为常见。年龄分布呈现双峰模式,峰值出现在20-29岁(38.53%)和60-69岁(29.55%)。中等病毒载量最常见(40.08%);HPV31和HPV16的高病毒载量比例最高,而HPV52则表现出“高患病率-低病毒载量”模式。高病毒载量比例随着感染复杂性的增加而增加。全年 患病率 范围为 17.9% 至 22.0%,2020 年最低。在大流行阶段,总体 患病率 分别为 20.53%、19.40% 和 19.88%,而多种感染率从 27.39% 连续下降至 21.65%。结论 北京女性HR-HPV感染以HPV52、HPV58、HPV16为主,年龄分布呈双峰分布,病毒载量具有基因型特异性。与大流行相关的总体 患病率 下降和多种类型感染的持续下降强调了大流行后时代有针对性的 疫苗接种 和筛查策略的重要性。

title: Efficient high-risk human papillomavirus screening through pooled testing: a simulation study based on real-world data in low- and middle-income countries
abstract: BACKGROUND: The World Health Organization recommends high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) testing as the primary method for cervical cancer screening. Combining samples in a pool can reduce the expense associated with large numbers of commercially available tests. This study simulated the potential test-saving impact of pooled hrHPV testing using real-world data from two low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). METHODS: We simulated a two- and three-stage hrHPV pooling in Bangladesh (hrHPV prevalence 2.10%) and Uganda (hrHPV prevalence 22.52%) using real-world laboratory data. Measurements included the number of tests per stage, the total number of tests, and the percentage of tests saved. We performed sensitivity analysis to assess the impact of a 1.00% loss of sensitivity and specificity per additional sample in the pool on the false-negative rate (FNR). RESULTS: In Bangladesh, the two-stage strategy (eight samples per pool) and the three-stage strategy saved 71.21% and 77.21% of tests, respectively, compared to testing individually. In Uganda, the two-stage strategy (three samples per pool) reduced the number of tests by 15.34% compared to testing individually. Assuming loss of sensitivity and specificity due to pooling, the FNR was higher (FNR = 0.012-0.134) when hrHPV prevalence was low under the two-stage strategy. CONCLUSIONS: Pooled hrHPV testing has the potential to reduce the number of tests used and enhance screening capacity in resource-limited settings. Notably, a lower prevalence of hrHPV allows for more efficient pooled testing. Despite the potential loss of sensitivity and specificity, pooled hrHPV testing could offer benefits for LMICs and warrant further verification.

analysis.summary_en: This simulation study evaluated the potential of pooled high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) testing to reduce test costs in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Using real-world data from Bangladesh (hrHPV prevalence 2.10%) and Uganda (22.52%), the study simulated two- and three-stage pooling strategies. In Bangladesh, the two-stage strategy saved 71.21% of tests, while the three-stage strategy saved 77.21%. In Uganda, the two-stage strategy reduced tests by 15.34%. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 世界卫生组织建议将高风险 人乳头瘤病毒 (hrHPV) 检测作为 宫颈癌 筛查的主要方法,并将样本合并到一个池中可以减少与大量商用检测相关的费用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项研究使用来自两个低收入和中等收入国家 (LMIC) 的真实数据模拟了合并 hrHPV 检测的潜在测试节省影响。
elements_zh.methods: 我们使用真实实验室数据模拟了孟加拉国 (hrHPV 患病率 2.10%) 和乌干达 (hrHPV 患病率 22.52%) 的两阶段和三阶段 hrHPV 合并,进行了敏感性分析,以评估池中每个额外样本敏感性和特异性损失 1.00% 对假阴性率 (FNR) 的影响,并测量了每个阶段的测试次数、测试总数、以及保存的测试的百分比。
elements_zh.main_results: 在孟加拉国,与单独测试相比,两阶段策略(每个池 8 个样本)和三阶段策略分别节省了 71.21% 和 77.21% 的测试次数;在乌干达,两阶段策略(每个池三个样本)与单独测试相比,减少了15.34%的测试数量;假设由于合并而导致敏感性和特异性损失,在两阶段策略下,当 hrHPV 患病率 较低时,FNR 较高 (FNR = 0.012-0.134)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 合并 hrHPV 检测有可能减少所使用的检测数量并增强资源有限环境中的筛查能力,值得注意的是,较低的 hrHPV 患病率 可以实现更有效的合并检测。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 合并 hrHPV 检测可以通过降低检测成本和提高筛查能力为低收入和中等收入国家带来好处,尽管可能会损失敏感性和特异性,但仍需要进一步验证。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是基于真实世界数据的模拟,由于合并可能会损失敏感性和特异性,因此证据强度中等,这可能会影响假阴性率,特别是在低 患病率 设置中。

title: Rewired DDR-TGF-β-β-catenin-PD-L1 axis accelerates progression and shapes therapy in human papillomavirus-driven cancer
abstract: Understanding Human papillomavirus (HPV) oncogenic mechanisms is essential for developing preventive and therapeutic strategies and overcoming therapy resistance in HPV-related cancers. These challenges may arise from the ability of high-risk HPV to subvert host tumor suppressors such as p53 and Rb, and to drive oncogenesis through homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) and multi-network dysregulation. Mechanistically, HPV exerts context-dependent effects on the host DNA damage response (DDR). During episomal replication, E6/E7 activate DDR and recruit BRCA1/RAD51 to replication foci to support viral replication without significantly compromising host HR repair. Upon viral integration, however, sustained E6/E7 expression drives HRD and shifts DNA repair toward error-prone end joining, generating genomic instability that fuels malignant transformation. These alterations are most clearly established in cervical cancer, whereas evidence in HPV-positive non-cervical cancer is more variable and requires further context-specific validation. In parallel, HPV E6/E7 antagonize transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β)-mediated tumor suppression and, potentially through FAT Atypical Cadherin 4 (FAT4) down-regulation, engage Wnt/β-catenin signaling. The resultant elevation of nuclear β-catenin induces programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression promotes immune evasion, stemness, and invasiveness. Of note, while the DDR-TGF-β-β-catenin-PD-L1 axis is backed by substantial evidence in HPV-related cancers, certain connections within this pathway are extrapolated from non-HPV models or general pathway biology and are explicitly denoted as such in the main text. With residual p53 activity, HRD may confer initial sensitivity to DNA-damaging agents, but resistance frequently develops—a pattern reminiscent of the initial response followed by acquired resistance observed with immunotherapies in HPV-related cancers. Integrating these mechanistic insights, we propose ablative therapies (e.g., ablation, photodynamic therapy, surgery) for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN), and for advanced or resistant disease, a synthetic-lethality framework combining genotoxic therapies with DDR inhibitors, targeting DDR-TGF-β-β-catenin-PD-L1 axis, and antiviral approaches. The proposed therapeutic strategies, however, should be interpreted with caution, as their evidence base varies across tumor types and warrants further investigation.

analysis.study_design_and_population: These challenges may arise from the ability of high-risk HPV to subvert host tumor suppressors such as p53 and Rb, and to drive oncogenesis through homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) and multi-network dysregulation.
analysis.methods: Mechanistically, HPV exerts context-dependent effects on the host DNA damage response (DDR).
analysis.main_results: During episomal replication, E6/E7 activate DDR and recruit BRCA1/RAD51 to replication foci to support viral replication without significantly compromising host HR repair. Upon viral integration, however, sustained E6/E7 expression drives HRD and shifts DNA repair toward error-prone end joining, generating genomic instability that fuels malignant transformation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These alterations are most clearly established in cervical cancer, whereas evidence in HPV-positive non-cervical cancer is more variable and requires further context-specific validation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Integrating these mechanistic insights, we propose ablative therapies (e.g., ablation, photodynamic therapy, surgery) for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN), and for advanced or resistant disease, a synthetic-lethality framework combining genotoxic therapies with DDR inhibitors, targeting DDR-TGF-β-β-catenin-PD-L1 axis, and antiviral approaches.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The proposed therapeutic strategies, however, should be interpreted with caution, as their evidence base varies across tumor types and warrants further investigation.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the oncogenic mechanisms of human papillomavirus (HPV), focusing on its role in subverting host tumor suppressors and driving genomic instability through DDR and multi-network dysregulation. It highlights the context-dependent effects of HPV on the DNA damage response (DDR), particularly during episomal replication and viral integration. The research identifies the DDR-TGF-β-β-catenin-PD-L1 axis as a key pathway in HPV-related cancers, with implications for therapeutic strategies such as ablative therapies and synthetic-lethality approaches. However, the evidence base for these strategies varies across tumor types, necessitating further investigation. The findings emphasize the need for context-specific validation, especially in non-cervical HPV-positive cancers, and underscore the importance of understanding HPV's impact on immune evasion and malignant transformation.

title_zh: 重新连线的 DDR-TGF-β-β-连环蛋白-PD-L1 轴可加速 人乳头瘤病毒 驱动的癌症的进展并塑造治疗方法
source_body_en: Understanding Human papillomavirus (HPV) oncogenic mechanisms is essential for developing preventive and therapeutic strategies and overcoming therapy resistance in HPV-related cancers. These challenges may arise from the ability of high-risk HPV to subvert host tumor suppressors such as p53 and Rb, and to drive oncogenesis through homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) and multi-network dysregulation. Mechanistically, HPV exerts context-dependent effects on the host DNA damage response (DDR). During episomal replication, E6/E7 activate DDR and recruit BRCA1/RAD51 to replication foci to support viral replication without significantly compromising host HR repair. Upon viral integration, however, sustained E6/E7 expression drives HRD and shifts DNA repair toward error-prone end joining, generating genomic instability that fuels malignant transformation. These alterations are most clearly established in cervical cancer, whereas evidence in HPV-positive non-cervical cancer is more variable and requires further context-specific validation. In parallel, HPV E6/E7 antagonize transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β)-mediated tumor suppression and, potentially through FAT Atypical Cadherin 4 (FAT4) down-regulation, engage Wnt/β-catenin signaling. The resultant elevation of nuclear β-catenin induces programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression promotes immune evasion, stemness, and invasiveness. Of note, while the DDR-TGF-β-β-catenin-PD-L1 axis is backed by substantial evidence in HPV-related cancers, certain connections within this pathway are extrapolated from non-HPV models or general pathway biology and are explicitly denoted as such in the main text. With residual p53 activity, HRD may confer initial sensitivity to DNA-damaging agents, but resistance frequently develops—a pattern reminiscent of the initial response followed by acquired resistance observed with immunotherapies in HPV-related cancers. Integrating these mechanistic insights, we propose ablative therapies (e.g., ablation, photodynamic therapy, surgery) for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN), and for advanced or resistant disease, a synthetic-lethality framework combining genotoxic therapies with DDR inhibitors, targeting DDR-TGF-β-β-catenin-PD-L1 axis, and antiviral approaches. The proposed therapeutic strategies, however, should be interpreted with caution, as their evidence base varies across tumor types and warrants further investigation.
abstract_zh: 了解 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 致癌机制对于制定预防和治疗策略以及克服 HPV 相关癌症的治疗耐药性至关重要。这些挑战可能源于 高危型HPV 颠覆 宿主 肿瘤抑制因子(如 p53 和 Rb)的能力,并通过同源重组缺陷(HRD)和多网络失调驱动肿瘤发生。从机制上讲,HPV 对 宿主 DNA 损伤反应 (DDR) 产生环境依赖性影响。在附加型复制过程中,E6/E7 激活 DDR 并将 BRCA1/RAD51 招募到复制灶以支持病毒复制,而不会显着损害 宿主 HR 修复。然而,在病毒整合后,持续的 E6/E7 表达会驱动 HRD 并将 DNA 修复转向容易出错的末端连接,从而产生基因组不稳定,从而加剧恶性转化。这些改变在 宫颈癌 中最为明确,而 HPV 阳性非 宫颈癌 中的证据变化更大,需要进一步针对具体情况进行验证。与此同时,HPV E6/E7 拮抗转化生长因子-β (TGF-β) 介导的肿瘤抑制,并可能通过 FAT 非典型钙粘蛋白 4 (FAT4) 下调,参与 Wnt/β-连环蛋白信号传导。由此产生的核 β-连环蛋白升高会诱导程序性死亡配体 1 (PD-L1) 表达,从而促进免疫逃避、干性和侵袭性。值得注意的是,虽然 DDR-TGF-β-β-连环蛋白-PD-L1 轴得到 HPV 相关癌症的大量证据支持,但该通路内的某些联系是从非 HPV 模型或一般通路生物学推断出来的,并在正文中明确指出。凭借残留的 p53 活性,HRD 可能会赋予对 DNA 损伤剂的初始敏感性,但经常会产生耐药性,这种模式让人想起在 HPV 相关癌症的免疫疗法中观察到的初始反应,然后是获得性耐药。整合这些机制见解,我们提出了针对宫颈上皮内瘤变 (CIN) 的消融疗法(例如消融、光动力疗法、手术),以及针对晚期或耐药性疾病,提出了一种将基因毒性疗法与 DDR 抑制剂相结合、靶向 DDR-TGF-β-β-catenin-PD-L1 轴的合成致死框架,以及 抗病毒药物 方法。然而,所提出的治疗策略应谨慎解释,因为其证据基础因肿瘤类型而异,需要进一步研究。

title: The Role of Pneumococcal and Human Papillomavirus Vaccination in Preventing Otolaryngological Diseases: Implications for Pediatric Practice
abstract: Vaccinations are a cornerstone of primary prevention in pediatric otolaryngology and play a critical role in reducing the burden of pediatric infectious diseases, particularly acute otitis media (AOM) and HPV-related infections. The introduction and widespread use of pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCVs) have been associated with substantial changes in the epidemiology of pediatric AOM, particularly through reductions in vac-cine-serotype disease and complicated forms, while contributing to changes in pathogen distribution with an increased role of non-vaccine serotypes and non-pneumococcal bac-teria, requiring continuous epidemiological surveillance. Prophylactic human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination in adolescents and young adults effectively prevents oral infection with vaccine-type high-risk HPV, a necessary step in the pathogenesis of HPV-related oropharyngeal carcinoma. Clinical and epidemiological studies demonstrate robust antibody responses and significant reductions in oral HPV prevalence among vaccinated individuals. Although direct evidence of a reduction in oropharyngeal cancer incidence is not yet available, vaccination may consequently reduce the future burden of HPV-related oropharyngeal cancers. Long-term surveillance remains essential to confirm this potential benefit. Barriers to optimal vaccine coverage include unequal access, incomplete vaccination uptake, and limited awareness of HPV-related oral disease. In conclusion, vaccinations provide direct and clinically relevant benefits in pediatric otolaryngology by reducing recurrent AOM, severe complications and surgical interventions. HPV vaccination also reduces vaccine-type oral HPV infection and may consequently contribute to reducing the future burden of HPV-related oropharyngeal cancers. Achieving high vaccination coverage, coupled with continuous epidemiological monitoring, is essential to maximize individual and public health benefits and to inform the development of vaccines with broader serotype coverage.

The introduction and widespread use of pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCVs) have been associated with substantial changes in the epidemiology of pediatric AOM, particularly through reductions in vac-cine-serotype disease and complicated forms, while contributing to changes in pathogen distribution with an increased role of non-vaccine serotypes and non-pneumococcal bac-teria, requiring continuous epidemiological surveillance. Prophylactic human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination in adolescents and young adults effectively prevents oral infection with vaccine-type high-risk HPV, a necessary step in the pathogenesis of HPV-related oropharyngeal carcinoma. Clinical and epidemiological studies demonstrate robust antibody responses and significant reductions in oral HPV prevalence among vaccinated individuals. Although direct evidence of a reduction in oropharyngeal cancer incidence is not yet available, vaccination may consequently reduce the future burden of HPV-related oropharyngeal cancers. Long-term surveillance remains essential to confirm this potential benefit. Barriers to optimal vaccine coverage include unequal access, incomplete vaccination uptake, and limited awareness of HPV-related oral disease. In conclusion, vaccinations provide direct and clinically relevant benefits in pediatric otolaryngology by reducing recurrent AOM, severe complications and surgical interventions. HPV vaccination also reduces vaccine-type oral HPV infection and may consequently contribute to reducing the future burden of HPV-related oropharyngeal cancers. Achieving high vaccination coverage, coupled with continuous epidemiological monitoring, is essential to maximize individual and public health benefits and to inform the development of vaccines with broader serotype coverage.

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是一项概念性综述,重点关注 HPV 疫苗接种 的演变情况,未提供具体的研究设计或人群详细信息。

analysis_zh.main_results: 该研究强调了当前 疫苗 疗效指标的局限性,并提出重新定义 HPV 疫苗接种 的目标和策略。

title: Awareness, factual knowledge, attitudes, and acceptability of human papillomavirus vaccination among adult women in Palestine: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a major preventable cause of cervical cancer, yet awareness and uptake of HPV vaccination remain suboptimal in many settings. Evidence regarding women's HPV-related awareness, factual knowledge, and vaccine acceptability in Palestine remains limited. This study assessed awareness, factual knowledge, attitudes, self-reported uptake, willingness, and perceived barriers related to HPV infection and HPV vaccination among adult women in Palestine. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted between October 2025 and February 2026 among women aged ≥18 years residing in Palestine. The questionnaire assessed sociodemographic characteristics, HPV and HPV vaccine awareness, factual knowledge, attitudes, vaccine uptake, willingness to receive or recommend vaccination, and perceived barriers. A 12-item factual knowledge score was calculated, and higher factual knowledge was defined as ≥7 correct responses. Descriptive statistics, subgroup analyses, and multivariable logistic regression were performed. Results Among 424 adult women included in the final analysis, 220 (51.9%) had heard of HPV and 146 (34.4%) had heard of the HPV vaccine. The mean factual knowledge score was 4.03 ± 2.72 out of 12, and 90 participants (21.2%) had higher factual knowledge. Self-reported HPV vaccine uptake was low (13.0%), whereas willingness to receive the vaccine was higher (55.2%). Lack of awareness (55.8%) and concern about vaccine safety (22.8%) were the most frequently reported barriers among unvaccinated women. In expanded adjusted analyses, prior HPV awareness, prior HPV vaccine awareness, and more supportive HPV-vaccination attitudes were independently associated with higher factual knowledge. Higher factual knowledge and supportive attitudes were associated with self-reported vaccine uptake, while willingness among unvaccinated women was most strongly associated with supportive vaccination attitudes. Conclusion Adult women in Palestine demonstrated limited HPV-related awareness and low factual knowledge, together with low self-reported HPV vaccine uptake. The gap between willingness and uptake, combined with the predominance of awareness and safety concerns as reported barriers, suggests a need for culturally appropriate education, provider-led counseling, and improved access to reliable HPV vaccine information. Findings should be interpreted cautiously given the cross-sectional design and online convenience sampling.

The questionnaire assessed sociodemographic characteristics, HPV and HPV vaccine awareness, factual knowledge, attitudes, vaccine uptake, willingness to receive or recommend vaccination, and perceived barriers. A 12-item factual knowledge score was calculated, and higher factual knowledge was defined as ≥7 correct responses. Descriptive statistics, subgroup analyses, and multivariable logistic regression were performed. Results Among 424 adult women included in the final analysis, 220 (51.9%) had heard of HPV and 146 (34.4%) had heard of the HPV vaccine. The mean factual knowledge score was 4.03 ± 2.72 out of 12, and 90 participants (21.2%) had higher factual knowledge. Self-reported HPV vaccine uptake was low (13.0%), whereas willingness to receive the vaccine was higher (55.2%). Lack of awareness (55.8%) and concern about vaccine safety (22.8%) were the most frequently reported barriers among unvaccinated women. In expanded adjusted analyses, prior HPV awareness, prior HPV vaccine awareness, and more supportive HPV-vaccination attitudes were independently associated with higher factual knowledge. Higher factual knowledge and supportive attitudes were associated with self-reported vaccine uptake, while willingness among unvaccinated women was most strongly associated with supportive vaccination attitudes. Conclusion Adult women in Palestine demonstrated limited HPV-related awareness and low factual knowledge, together with low self-reported HPV vaccine uptake. The gap between willingness and uptake, combined with the predominance of awareness and safety concerns as reported barriers, suggests a need for culturally appropriate education, provider-led counseling, and improved access to reliable HPV vaccine information. Findings should be interpreted cautiously given the cross-sectional design and online convenience sampling.
