title: Comparison of Ex-House and In-House Cytology for the New Cervical Cancer Screening Assessment
abstract: Abstract The introduction of an organized cervical cancer screening program in Germany in 2020 changed screening algorithms and referral patterns, increasing the number of patients referred to specialized centers. This study examines the concordance between ex-house Pap smear findings and in-house colposcopy-guided cytology and relates both to colposcopy-guided biopsy and histopathological outcomes within the new screening program. In this retrospective study, data from 3161 patients referred for colposcopy to a certified university dysplasia unit between January 2020 and May 2024 were analyzed. All patients underwent standardized assessment including Pap smear, HPV testing, colposcopy, and colposcopy-guided biopsy, with surgical treatment when indicated. Concordance between ex-house and in-house cytology was moderate (Spearman’s ρ = 0.453, p < 0.001; weighted Cohen’s κ = 0.581). Compared with histology, ex-house cytology showed overdiagnosis in 252 cases (14.29%), underdiagnosis in 631 cases (35.79%), and concordant findings in 880 cases (49.91%). In contrast, in-house cytology demonstrated lower rates of overdiagnosis (183 cases, 9.48%) and underdiagnosis (495 cases, 25.65%), with agreement in 1252 cases (64.87%). HPV positivity increased with cytological severity, with HPV16 being the most prevalent genotype in high-grade lesions. Among low-grade cytological findings, CIN3+ yield differed markedly according to HPV status. In the setting of the cervical cancer screening program, in-house cytology performed in a specialized dysplasia unit demonstrated closer agreement with histology than ex-house cytology. HPV status emerged as a key modifier of risk within low-grade cytological categories, highlighting the importance of risk-adapted triage and reassessment colposcopy in contemporary screening practice.

In the setting of the cervical cancer screening program, in-house cytology performed in a specialized dysplasia unit demonstrated closer agreement with histology than ex-house cytology. title: Local carboxymethyl-β-glucan and polycarbophil therapy is associated with regression of low-grade cervical cytological abnormalities: a prospective observational study
abstract: Aim: To evaluate the association between intravaginal therapy with carboxymethyl-β-glucan (CMBG) and polycarbophil and cytological regression of atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASCUS) and cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 1 (CIN 1), compared with standard follow-up. Methods: This prospective observational controlled study included 80 women aged 23–49 years with ASCUS or CIN 1. Forty patients received intravaginal CMBG/polycarbophil spray, and 40 were managed with standard follow-up. Allocation was based on clinical assessment and therapy availability, without randomisation. The primary outcome was cytological normalisation after 12 months, based on Papanicolaou smear results. Results: After 12 months, abnormal cytology was observed in 4 (10.0%) patients in the treatment group and 18 (45.0%) in the control group (RR 0.22; 95% CI 0.08–0.60; p<0.001). Normal cytology was observed in 36 (90.0%) and 22 (55.0%) patients, respectively (p<0.001). Human papillomavirus (HPV) persistence was detected in 2 (5.0%) patients in the treatment group and 5 (12.5%) in the control group (p=0.432). Conclusion: Intravaginal CMBG/polycarbophil therapy was associated with a higher rate of cytological normalisation than standard follow-up in women with ASCUS and CIN 1.

title: CONSTRUCCIÓN DE UN SISTEMA RECOMBINANTE EN ESCHERICHIA COLI BL21 861 CON EL GEN L1 DEL VIRUS DEL PAPILOMA HUMANO COMO CONTROL POSITIVO EN DIAGNÓSTICO MOLECULAR
abstract: Reliable positive controls are essential for the molecular diagnosis of Human Papillomavirus (HPV). In this study, a recombinant system based on Escherichia coli BL21 861 containing a ~450 bp fragment of the HPV L1 gene was developed as a biosafe positive control for PCR assays. The construct was designed in silico using MY09/MY11 target regions and cloned into a plasmid vector through restriction digestion and ligation. The recombinant plasmid was transformed into E. coli BL21 861, and successful insertion was confirmed by PCR and agarose gel electrophoresis. The developed system represents a stable and reproducible alternative for HPV molecular diagnostics, reducing dependence on clinical samples and improving assay standardization.

title: HPV vaccination and the risk of cancer in males
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The efficacy and effectiveness of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine in reducing the risk of invasive cervical cancer in females and head and neck cancer (HNC) in males have been demonstrated. However, the relationship between HPV vaccination in males and the subsequent risk of other potentially HPV-associated cancers are lacking. METHODS: We used the TriNetX United States Collaborative Network to conduct a retrospective cohort study. Males aged 9 to 45 years who did or did not receive the HPV vaccine between 2006 and 2024 were included. We assessed the association between HPV vaccination and the risk of cancer, carcinoma in situ, and precancerous lesions at: penis, anus, head and neck cancer (HNC), lungs, esophagus, stomach, prostate, colorectum. RESULTS: Males with HPV vaccination (n = 397,856) have lower hazard ratio (HR) for HNC. Some other potentially HPV-associated cancers also have lower HR in HPV-vaccinated males, including lung cancer, prostate cancer, and colorectal cancer. Vaccinated males were less likely to develop some precancerous lesions of anus, head and neck, esophagus, and stomach. CONCLUSIONS: Among males ages 9 to 45, HPV vaccination significantly reduces the risk of certain cancers and precancerous lesions. Further studies are needed to evaluate the protective mechanisms of HPV vaccination against various cancers.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of evidence regarding the relationship between HPV vaccination in males and the risk of potentially HPV-associated cancers beyond head and neck cancer.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX United States Collaborative Network, including males aged 9 to 45 years who did or did not receive the HPV vaccine between 2006 and 2024.
analysis.methods: The study assessed the association between HPV vaccination and the risk of cancer, carcinoma in situ, and precancerous lesions at multiple anatomical sites using hazard ratio analysis.
analysis.main_results: Males with HPV vaccination (n = 397,856) had a lower hazard ratio for head and neck cancer, as well as for lung cancer, prostate cancer, and colorectal cancer; vaccinated males were also less likely to develop precancerous lesions of the anus, head and neck, esophagus, and stomach.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that HPV vaccination significantly reduces the risk of certain cancers and precancerous lesions in males, representing a novel finding beyond established associations with cervical cancer in females and head and neck cancer in males.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the expansion of HPV vaccination recommendations to males for the prevention of a broader range of HPV-associated cancers and precancerous lesions, potentially reducing cancer burden and healthcare costs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Further studies are needed to evaluate the protective mechanisms of HPV vaccination against various cancers; the evidence strength is moderate due to the retrospective design and the need for additional mechanistic research.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cohort study investigated the association between HPV vaccination and cancer risk in males aged 9 to 45 years using the TriNetX United States Collaborative Network. Among 397,856 vaccinated males, significantly lower hazard ratios were observed for head and neck cancer, as well as for lung, prostate, and colorectal cancers. Vaccinated males also showed reduced risk of precancerous lesions in the anus, head and neck, esophagus, and stomach. The findings demonstrate that HPV vaccination significantly reduces the risk of multiple potentially HPV-associated cancers and precancerous lesions in males, extending beyond the previously established benefits for cervical cancer in females and head and neck cancer in males. While the results support broader vaccination recommendations, further research is needed to elucidate the protective mechanisms against various cancers.

title_zh: HPV 疫苗接种 与男性患癌症的风险
source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: The efficacy and effectiveness of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine in reducing the risk of invasive cervical cancer in females and head and neck cancer (HNC) in males have been demonstrated. However, the relationship between HPV vaccination in males and the subsequent risk of other potentially HPV-associated cancers are lacking. METHODS: We used the TriNetX United States Collaborative Network to conduct a retrospective cohort study. Males aged 9 to 45 years who did or did not receive the HPV vaccine between 2006 and 2024 were included. We assessed the association between HPV vaccination and the risk of cancer, carcinoma in situ, and precancerous lesions at: penis, anus, head and neck cancer (HNC), lungs, esophagus, stomach, prostate, colorectum. RESULTS: Males with HPV vaccination (n = 397,856) have lower hazard ratio (HR) for HNC. Some other potentially HPV-associated cancers also have lower HR in HPV-vaccinated males, including lung cancer, prostate cancer, and colorectal cancer. Vaccinated males were less likely to develop some precancerous lesions of anus, head and neck, esophagus, and stomach. CONCLUSIONS: Among males ages 9 to 45, HPV vaccination significantly reduces the risk of certain cancers and precancerous lesions. Further studies are needed to evaluate the protective mechanisms of HPV vaccination against various cancers.

title: A wiser way to approach anal cancer in women
abstract: A wiser way to approach anal cancer in women We hear from contributors from The University of Sydney’s Cancer Care Research Unit about the challenges faced by women with anal cancer and a study highlighting the need for better education and communication in addressing women’s sexual health concerns. Rates of anal cancer are increasing worldwide and disproportionately affect women, who account for over 60% of cases diagnosed each year. (1) Their unique anatomical characteristics are central to understanding the higher incidence rate. Firstly, the squamocolumnar junction, the most vulnerable part of the anal canal, is closer to the surface of the skin in females than in males. This makes the anus more susceptible to infection. Secondly, the unique anatomical structure of the female genital region is conducive for casual spread of the human papillomavirus (HPV) infection between the cervix, vagina, vulva, and anus. Over 90% of anal cancers diagnosed worldwide are associated with HPV.

title: Integrative multi-omics analysis identifies FAM3D as a prognostic tumor suppressor in cervical cancer
abstract: Cervical cancer (CC) remains a leading malignancy among women worldwide. Epigenetic and transcriptional dysregulation complicate the identification of causal genes with prognostic and therapeutic relevance. We performed a multi-omics integrative analysis combining summary data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR) using eQTL and pQTL datasets with genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics (ID: ukb-b-8777) to prioritize candidate genes associated with CC. Differential expression analyses were conducted using multiple GEO cohorts, and protein expression was validated by immunohistochemistry (IHC) in clinical specimens. DNA methylation profiling and correlation analyses were performed using GEO and TCGA datasets to investigate epigenetic regulation. Kaplan-Meier and combined expression-methylation survival analyses were used to evaluate prognostic significance. Functional validation was conducted in HeLa cells using wound-healing and CCK-8 assays following FAM3D knockdown or overexpression. RNA sequencing was further performed to explore the downstream molecular pathways regulated by FAM3D. Integrative SMR analysis identified FAM3D as a protective gene for CC. FAM3D expression was significantly reduced in CC tissues and exhibited a progressive decline from normal cervical tissues to cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) and invasive CC, which was further confirmed by IHC. Promoter hypermethylation of FAM3D (cg26334888) was associated with its transcriptional downregulation and negatively correlated with gene expression. Survival analyses demonstrated that high FAM3D expression (p = 0.016) and low promoter methylation (p = 0.048) were associated with favorable overall survival, while combined expression-methylation analysis further improved prognostic stratification (p = 0.006). Functional assays showed that FAM3D suppressed CC cell proliferation and migration. Transcriptomic profiling revealed that FAM3D restoration induced extensive transcriptional reprogramming and was associated with inflammatory signaling, cytokine-mediated pathways, and extracellular matrix remodeling. Key hub genes identified downstream of FAM3D included CXCL8, MMP1, EREG, and LCN2. FAM3D is a potential tumor suppressor and prognostic biomarker in CC, whose expression is partially regulated by promoter methylation. Integrative multi-omics analyses and functional studies suggest that FAM3D may inhibit CC progression through modulation of inflammatory signaling and extracellular matrix-associated pathways. These findings provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying CC and support the potential clinical utility of FAM3D as a prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target.

title: Squamous papilloma of the external ear in Southwest China: A large case series highlighting predominant HPV subtypes, pathologic features, and unique epidemiologic factors.
abstract: Squamous papilloma (SP) of the external ear is a rare benign neoplasm, with limited research on its associated human papillomavirus (HPV) infections and pathologic features. This study aims to provide a comprehensive analysis of the largest case series of external ear SP from Southwest China. We retrospectively collected 88 cases diagnosed with SP in the external ear canal, of which 85 (97%) were located in the external auditory canal and 3 (3%) on the auricle. We investigated the clinical, pathological, and HPV-typing characteristics using Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and reverse dot blot (RDB) hybridization. Our series included 74 males and 14 females, with a median age of 62.5 years (range: 5-91 years). The predominant HPV type was HPV-6 (59/62, 95.2%), followed by high-risk types HPV-16 (4/62, 6.5%), HPV-52 (2/62, 3.2%), and HPV-58 (1/62, 1.6%). Histologically, all cases demonstrated typical features of SP, including koilocytes, hyperkeratosis, and basal/parabasal hyperplasia. Additionally, co-infection with multiple HPV types was observed in four cases. Notably, high-risk HPV types were detected in seven cases, all of which were completely excised with no recurrence during follow-up. This study suggests regional variations in HPV-subtype distribution and highlights potential environmental factors contributing to the prevalence of SP in Southwest China.

source_records.title: Squamous papilloma of the external ear in Southwest China: A large case series highlighting predominant HPV subtypes, pathologic features, and unique epidemiologic factors.
source_records.abstract: Squamous papilloma (SP) of the external ear is a rare benign neoplasm, with limited research on its associated human papillomavirus (HPV) infections and pathologic features. This study aims to provide a comprehensive analysis of the largest case series of external ear SP from Southwest China. We retrospectively collected 88 cases diagnosed with SP in the external ear canal, of which 85 (97%) were located in the external auditory canal and 3 (3%) on the auricle. We investigated the clinical, pathological, and HPV-typing characteristics using Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and reverse dot blot (RDB) hybridization. Our series included 74 males and 14 females, with a median age of 62.5 years (range: 5-91 years). The predominant HPV type was HPV-6 (59/62, 95.2%), followed by high-risk types HPV-16 (4/62, 6.5%), HPV-52 (2/62, 3.2%), and HPV-58 (1/62, 1.6%). Histologically, all cases demonstrated typical features of SP, including koilocytes, hyperkeratosis, and basal/parabasal hyperplasia. Additionally, co-infection with multiple HPV types was observed in four cases. Notably, high-risk HPV types were detected in seven cases, all of which were completely excised with no recurrence during follow-up. This study suggests regional variations in HPV-subtype distribution and highlights potential environmental factors contributing to the prevalence of SP in Southwest China.

title: Multiple bovine papillomavirus types in squamous papillomas of the upper gastrointestinal tract of dairy cows from southern Brazil
abstract: Papillomavirus is an oncogenic virus that infects the cutaneous and mucosal epithelia of several host species. This study investigated the diversity of bovine papillomavirus (BPV) types in hyperplastic lesions of the esophageal mucosa in dairy cows from Paraná State, southern Brazil. A total of 23 hyperproliferative lesions were collected from the esophagus of 16 dairy cows and histologically classified as squamous papillomas. Consensual primer pairs FAP59/FAP64, MY11/MY09, and E1F2/E1R4 were used to partially amplify the L1 and E1 genes of BPVs. Amplicons were sequenced using the Sanger method. BPV DNA was detected in 21.7% (5/23) of the esophageal lesions. Sequence analysis identified BPV types 1 and 4, previously associated with such lesions, in two lesions. BPV types 9 and 40 were detected for the first time in mucosal lesions of the upper gastrointestinal tract (UGT) in two additional samples. Furthermore, one lesion contained DNA from a putative novel BPV type phylogenetically related to BPV12. Overall, five distinct BPV types were molecularly detected across five lesions. These findings suggest that, similar to cutaneous papillomatosis, multiple BPV types may be associated with papillomas in the esophageal mucosa of dairy cows, particularly those raised on bracken fern–contaminated pastures. The study highlights the importance of utilizing multiple consensual primer sets targeting conserved regions of the L1 and E1 genes to more accurately characterize BPV diversity in mucosal lesions, as novel and previously unreported viral types may be present.
authors: Ana Paula Frederico Rodrigues Loureiro Bracarense

title: Association of nasopharynx cancer with obstructive sleep apnea
abstract: Introduction Despite the extensive research conducted on the association between OSA and HNCs, the specific relationship between obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) has received comparatively less attention. The present study aimed to explore the association between OSA and NPC. Methods The data for this study was drawn from the Longitudinal Health Insurance Database 2010. The study incorporated a total of 3,235 NPC patients and 12,940 propensity score-matched controls. The NPC and controls’ baseline clinical and demographic parameters were compared using standardized mean difference. A conditional logistic regression model was developed in order to quantify the association between OSA and the odds of NPC. Results The prevalence of prior OSA was significantly higher in the NPC group than in the control group (2.07% vs. Following the adjustment for a comprehensive set of confounders, including age, sex, income, geography, urbanization, diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, COPD, chronic rhinitis, sinusitis, human papillomavirus infection, tobacco use disorder, and alcohol-related disorders, pre-existing OSA remained associated with an increased odds of developing NPC (adjusted OR = 1.42, 95% CI = 1.07, 1.89). In sex-stratified analysis, the point estimates for the association between OSA and NPC were similar for both males (adjusted OR = 1.41, 95% CI = 1.03, 1.94) and females (adjusted OR = 1.46, 95% CI = 0.77, 2.78). While the association only reached statistical significance in the males, the lack of significance in females may be indicative of lower statistical precision due to the smaller sample size. Conclusion The present study identifies an association between prior OSA diagnosis and NPC, particularly in the males. Further investigation is required to confirm this relationship and its underlying mechanisms.

title: Immortal Time Bias Can Reverse the Estimated Association: A Clone-Censor-Weight Analysis in an EHR-Based HPV Vaccination Target Trial Emulation
abstract: Using an electronic health record-based human papillomavirus vaccination example, we show that immortal time bias can reverse the direction of an estimated association. We link clone-censor-weight analysis to the potential outcome framework, assess censoring-weight stability, and demonstrate dependence-aware inference, providing practical guidance for longitudinal target trial emulation with treatment strategies defined during follow-up.

title: Machine learning-enabled smartphone CRISPR-Cas12a lateral flow platform for sensitive detection of circulating HPV DNA
abstract: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) is a major cause of cervical cancer, and improved point-of-care (POC) detection is critical for early intervention. Although PCR-based assays are highly sensitive, their reliance on centralized laboratory infrastructure limits accessibility in decentralized settings. CRISPR-Cas diagnostics combined with lateral flow assays (LFA) offer a rapid alternative; however, visual interpretation of faint test bands remains subjective and variable. Here, we developed a smartphone-based CRISPR-Cas12a LFA platform integrated with an interpretable machine learning (ML) framework for quantitative detection of circulating HPV DNA in plasma. Standardized image acquisition was implemented using a light-controlled enclosure, and radiomics-inspired features were analyzed using a multivariable logistic regression model. The system was trained on 150 plasma samples and validated in an independent cohort of 60 samples. The optimized model achieved 96.7% sensitivity and 100% specificity, outperforming visual interpretation, particularly for low-signal samples. Performance remained stable across different smartphone models, lighting conditions, and operators, with rapid on-device inference enabling consistent and reliable operation. This integrated CRISPR-LFA platform demonstrates accurate and reproducible detection of circulating HPV DNA and supports feasibility for POC applications, pending further validation in broader clinical settings.

full_text: Abstract Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is a major public health concern and a leading cause of cervical cancer among women worldwide. HPV vaccination remains an effective preventive strategy; however, vaccine acceptance among adolescents in low- and middle-income countries remains suboptimal. This study assessed factors associated with HPV vaccine acceptance among adolescent girls in selected public secondary schools in Abeokuta South Local Government Area, Ogun State, Nigeria. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 380 adolescent girls selected through a multistage sampling technique from two public secondary schools in Abeokuta South Local Government Area, Ogun State. Data were collected using a structured self-administered questionnaire. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS version 26. Descriptive statistics, chi-square test, Fisher’s exact test, and binary logistic regression were used for data analysis at a significance level of p < 0.05. Results The mean age of respondents was 15.46±.94years. More than half, 223 (58.7%) had heard of the HPV vaccine. Overall, 221 (41.8%) had good knowledge, 365 (96.1%) had good perception, and 285 (75.0%) demonstrated high acceptance of HPV vaccination. Bivariate analysis showed significant associations between HPV vaccine acceptance and age (p = 0.003), father’s education (p = 0.013), mother’s occupation (p = 0.030), father’s occupation (p < 0.001), living arrangement (p < 0.001), knowledge level (p = 0.005), and perception level (p = 0.003). Logistic regression analysis revealed that respondents aged 14–15 years (AOR = 2.81; 95% CI: 1.17–6.73), those whose mothers were professionals (AOR = 3.15; 95% CI: 1.42–6.99), and those with good knowledge and perception were more likely to accept HPV vaccination. Conversely, poor knowledge (AOR = 0.40; 95% CI: 0.22–0.76) and poor perception (AOR = 0.17; 95% CI: 0.04–0.76) significantly reduced the likelihood of vaccine acceptance. Conclusion Although acceptance of HPV vaccination among adolescent girls was relatively high, knowledge regarding HPV and its vaccine remained suboptimal. Knowledge, perception, parental characteristics, and living arrangement were significantly associated with reported HPV vaccine acceptance. Strengthening school-based health education and involving parents in HPV vaccine advocacy programs may improve informed acceptance and potentially support future vaccination uptake among adolescents. full_text_sections.full_text: Abstract Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is a major public health concern and a leading cause of cervical cancer among women worldwide. HPV vaccination remains an effective preventive strategy; however, vaccine acceptance among adolescents in low- and middle-income countries remains suboptimal. This study assessed factors associated with HPV vaccine acceptance among adolescent girls in selected public secondary schools in Abeokuta South Local Government Area, Ogun State, Nigeria. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 380 adolescent girls selected through a multistage sampling technique from two public secondary schools in Abeokuta South Local Government Area, Ogun State. Data were collected using a structured self-administered questionnaire. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS version 26. Descriptive statistics, chi-square test, Fisher’s exact test, and binary logistic regression were used for data analysis at a significance level of p < 0.05. Results The mean age of respondents was 15.46±.94years. More than half, 223 (58.7%) had heard of the HPV vaccine. Overall, 221 (41.8%) had good knowledge, 365 (96.1%) had good perception, and 285 (75.0%) demonstrated high acceptance of HPV vaccination. Bivariate analysis showed significant associations between HPV vaccine acceptance and age (p = 0.003), father’s education (p = 0.013), mother’s occupation (p = 0.030), father’s occupation (p < 0.001), living arrangement (p < 0.001), knowledge level (p = 0.005), and perception level (p = 0.003). Logistic regression analysis revealed that respondents aged 14–15 years (AOR = 2.81; 95% CI: 1.17–6.73), those whose mothers were professionals (AOR = 3.15; 95% CI: 1.42–6.99), and those with good knowledge and perception were more likely to accept HPV vaccination. Conversely, poor knowledge (AOR = 0.40; 95% CI: 0.22–0.76) and poor perception (AOR = 0.17; 95% CI: 0.04–0.76) significantly reduced the likelihood of vaccine acceptance. Conclusion Although acceptance of HPV vaccination among adolescent girls was relatively high, knowledge regarding HPV and its vaccine remained suboptimal. Knowledge, perception, parental characteristics, and living arrangement were significantly associated with reported HPV vaccine acceptance. Strengthening school-based health education and involving parents in HPV vaccine advocacy programs may improve informed acceptance and potentially support future vaccination uptake among adolescents. analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study investigated factors associated with HPV vaccine acceptance among 380 adolescent girls in Abeokuta South, Nigeria. While 75.0% showed high acceptance, knowledge remained suboptimal. Significant predictors included age (14-15 years), parental professional status, good knowledge, and positive perception. The study highlights the need for school-based health education and parental involvement to improve vaccination uptake. Limitations include the cross-sectional design, but the large sample size and robust analyses provide moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究评估了尼日利亚奥贡州阿贝奥库塔南地方政府区选定公立中学少女中 HPV 疫苗 接受度的相关因素,解决了低收入和中等收入国家 疫苗 接受度欠佳的问题。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对奥贡州阿贝奥库塔南地方政府区两所公立中学通过多阶段抽样技术选出的 380 名少女进行了一项横断面研究。
elements_zh.methods: 使用结构化自填问卷收集数据,并使用描述性统计、卡方检验、Fisher精确检验和二元逻辑回归进行数据分析,显着性水平为p < 0.05。
elements_zh.main_results: 总体而言,285 人 (75.0%) 对 HPV 疫苗接种 表现出较高的接受度,双变量分析显示 HPV 疫苗 接受度与年龄、父母教育和职业、生活安排、知识水平和认知水平之间存在显着相关性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 尽管青春期女孩对 HPV 疫苗接种 的接受度相对较高,但对 HPV 及其 疫苗 的了解仍然不够理想,知识、认知、父母特征和生活安排与报告的接受度显着相关。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 加强以学校为基础的健康教育并让家长参与 HPV 疫苗 宣传计划可能会提高知情接受度,并有可能支持未来青少年对 疫苗接种 的吸收。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是横断面的,限制了因果推断,但大样本量和严格的统计分析提供了中等的证据强度。

analysis_zh.methods: 使用结构化自填问卷收集数据,并使用描述性统计、卡方检验、Fisher精确检验和二元逻辑回归进行数据分析,显着性水平为p < 0.05。
analysis_zh.main_results: 总体而言,285 人 (75.0%) 对 HPV 疫苗接种 表现出较高的接受度,双变量分析显示 HPV 疫苗 接受度与年龄、父母教育和职业、生活安排、知识水平和认知水平之间存在显着相关性。

title: Attitudes and Knowledge About Human Papillomavirus and Cervical Cancer among Women Referred to a Tertiary Gynecologic Oncology Clinic, Tehran, Iran
abstract: Background & Objective: Cervical cancer is a major public health concern worldwide. This study was conducted with aim to assess the attitudes and knowledge about Human Papillomavirus (HPV) and cervical cancer among women attending a tertiary gynecologic clinic.Materials & Methods: This descriptive, cross-sectional survey was conducted among 139 women referred to the gynecologic clinics of Yas Hospital Complex, affiliated with Tehran University of Medical Sciences, from 2023 to 2024. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews. Data analysis was performed using SPSS (IBM SPSS Statistics for Windows, Version 25). P<0.05 was considered statistically significant.Results: The mean total knowledge score was 25.07±5.92 out of a possible 33 points. Participants demonstrated strong foundational awareness, correctly identifying HPV as a sexually transmitted infection, recognizing that HPV affects both genders, and recognizing its role in causing cervical cancer. However, knowledge of the risks of vertical transmission and the lack of a specific antiviral treatment for HPV was low. Educational attainment was significantly associated with knowledge levels (P=0.01). Indeed, educational attainment was the strongest predictor of knowledge scores.Conclusion: In this clinical setting, basic HPV awareness was high among women. However, substantial misconceptions persisted regarding treatment options, vertical transmission, and vaccination efficacy. These findings highlight an urgent need for educational interventions targeting these knowledge gaps, particularly among women with lower educational attainment. They also underscore the need for structured HPV education and culturally tailored awareness campaigns.

Introduction Cervical cancer is a major public health concern worldwide. It is the fourth most common cancer among women globally. In 2020, about 604 new cases and 342 deaths per 1000 occurred worldwide. Over 85% of these deaths occur in low- and middle-income countries. Preventive strategies, such as Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination and regular screening, remain underused in these areas (1-4). Knowledge gaps and attitudinal barriers continue to impede the implementation of preventive strategies. Among women in Iran, cervical cancer is the tenth most frequent cancer. It is the seventh most common among women aged 15-44 years. There is a lack of a national HPV vaccination program in Iran. Routine cervical cancer screening with Pap smears is not available everywhere (5). Additional barriers include cultural sensitivities around Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) and limited public awareness of HPV. Since knowledge and attitudes directly affect screening behaviors and Elham Shirali, et al. 684 Volume 11, August 2026 Journal of Obstetrics, Gynecology and Cancer Research vaccine acceptance, these factors reduce uptake of preventive measures (6,7). Significant problems include misconceptions about HPV transmission, infection-related stigma, and poor understanding of disease progression. These barriers are particularly strong in conservative societies like Iran. HPV awareness among university students, healthcare workers, and women in urban screening centers has been the focus of previous Iranian research. Ghojazadeh et al., (8) found that although most participants had heard of HPV, medical students in Tabriz had limited detailed knowledge of its transmission and complications. Pooyanmehr and Sarmadi (9) reported similar results in Kermanshah province. Persistent misconceptions about HPV persisted even among educated youth. However, few studies have specifically examined knowledge and attitudes among women actively using gynecologic oncology services. This group is at higher risk for HPV- related diseases and may be undergoing diagnostic or screening procedures. Therefore, the present study was conducted with aims to assess the attitude and knowledge about HPV and cervical cancer among women referred to a gynecological oncology clinic. 2. Materials and Methods This descriptive, cross-sectional survey was conducted among 139 women referred to the gynecologic clinics of Yas Hospital Complex, affiliated with Tehran University of Medical Sciences, from 2023 to 2024. During clinic visits, we recruited participants using non-probability convenience sampling. Women with a prior history of treating cervical lesions (such as cervical surgery and medication), a current pregnancy, prior HPV vaccination, or reluctance to participate in the study were excluded from the study. The sample size was estimated as 139 subjects according to the values reported in Wright et al., (11), a power of 80%, a significance level of 0.05. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews. A structured, previously validated questionnaire was used. The validity and internal consistency of the questionnaire was confirmedas 0.79 by Mojahed et al., (10). Demographic variables (age, marital status, education level, gravidity, parity, smoking/hookah history, and contraceptive methods) were addressed in separate sections. HPV infection knowledge was also assessed. This included its effects on different genders, prevalence and sexual transmission, the role of condom use in decreasing transmission, vertical transmission from mother to baby, related diseases (genital warts and cervical cancer), and knowledge of available treatment and vaccination. Responses were used to assess overall awareness and attitude. Statistical Analysis The data were analyzed using SPSS (IBM SPSS Statistics for Windows, Version 25.0, Armonk, NY). Continuous variables were presented as means±standard deviations. Categorical variables were presented as frequencies and percentages. One-way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) was used to compare knowledge scores across categorical variables (education level, marital status). Relationships between continuous variables (age, knowledge score) were assessed using the Pearson correlation coefficient. P<0.05 was considered statistically significant. 3. Results A total of 139 women participated in this study. The mean age of the participants was 36.92±10.00 years, with a range of 15 to 64 years. The largest group of participants (42.45%) held a bachelor's degree or higher. Most were married (69.8%), with a mean gravidity of 1.35±1.38 pregnancies. Most participants (65.5%) did not use contraception, while 23.7% used a condom. Smoking was reported by 10.1% of participants, and hookah use by 23.0%. The mean total knowledge score was 25.07±5.92 out of a maximum possible score of 33 points. Nearly all participants (92.8%) correctly identified HPV as a sexually transmitted infection. About 88% recognized that HPV infection affects both men and women. Knowledge of HPV's clinical implications was notably high. Most participants (83.5%) identified HPV as a cause of cervical cancer in women, and 84.9% knew of its association with genital warts. However, knowledge gaps were evident regarding vertical transmission. Only 42.4% were aware that HPV could be transmitted from mother to child during pregnancy or childbirth. Participants demonstrated a good understanding of prevention methods and risk factors. Most (76.3%) knew that condom use could reduce the risk of HPV transmission. Moreover, 90.6% correctly acknowledged that having multiple sexual partners increases the risk of infection. However, only 57.6% were aware that the early onset of sexual activity increases the risk of HPV infection. Knowledge of HPV treatment was limited. Only 31.7% correctly understood that no specific antiviral treatment exists for HPV infection. About 50% believed such treatment was available, an incorrect belief. Vaccination awareness was relatively high, with 86.3% agreeing that pre-sexual activity vaccination is preferable. However, only 54.0% believed that vaccination remains effective after sexual debut, while 36.0% were uncertain (Figure 1). Correlation analysis between age and overall knowledge score revealed no statistically significant relationship (r= -0.019, P=0.82). However, there was a significant correlation between educational attainment and knowledge levels (P=0.01). Educational attainment emerged as the strongest predictor of HPV knowledge. Women with higher diplomas had the 685 Attitudes and Knowledge about HPV Volume 11, August 2026 Journal of Obstetrics, Gynecology and Cancer Research highest knowledge scores. Across marital status categories, no statistically significant differences were found in knowledge scores (P=0.85) (Table 1). Figure 1. HPV Knowledge and Attitudes Table 1. Discussion The vast majority of participants demonstrated strong foundational HPV knowledge. Moreover, HPV was correctly identified as a sexually transmitted infection by 92.8%, and that it affects both men and women was recognized by 87.8%. These awareness levels are substantially higher than those reported in previous Iranian studies. In a study by Ghojazadeh et al., (8) among medical students in Tabriz found that 76% of students recognized STIs. Similar trends have been reported in international studies. Multiparous women demonstrate greater awareness of reproductive health risks. However, the non-significant association in our study indicates that healthcare providers should not assume that reproductive experience automatically confers HPV knowledge. Instead, these findings support the systematic integration of HPV education into routine maternal care visits (12). Behavioral risk factors revealed patterns linking lifestyle choices with deficits in health knowledge. In the present study, women with a smoking history (10.1%) and hookah use (23.0%) had lower HPV knowledge scores than non-users; however, the difference was not significant in our sample. This trend aligns with established research showing that tobacco users consistently have lower engagement with preventive health services and lower health literacy across multiple domains (13-15). Despite Iran's absence of a national HPV vaccination program, awareness regarding vaccination was high. The vaccine's preventive potential when administered before sexual debut was recognized by 86.3% of participants. This level of awareness suggests effective informal dissemination of health information. This may occur through healthcare providers, the media, or international health sources (16,17). An important association between protective behaviors and HPV knowledge was revealed by contraceptive use patterns. In the present study, women using barrier contraceptives, particularly condoms (23.7%), demonstrated slightly higher knowledge scores than non-users. That condom use reduces HPV transmission risk was correctly understood by 76.3%. This relationship between contraceptive choice and health knowledge likely reflects broader patterns of health-conscious behavior. Sexual health literacy and proactive healthcare engagement extend beyond contraception alone (18,19). However, a critical knowledge gap emerged regarding asymptomatic transmission dynamics. That HPV can be transmitted between carriers was correctly understood by 62.6% of participants in the current research. A concerning 38.8% misunderstood the potential for asymptomatic individuals to transmit the virus. About this mechanism, 30.9% were uncertain. This represents a fundamental misconception with significant implications for prevention behaviors. The majority of HPV infections are asymptomatic. Individuals may unknowingly transmit the virus to partners (20). This study's primary strength lies in its real-world clinical setting. It provides insights into HPV knowledge among women actively engaged in gynecologic care, a population at potentially heightened risk for HPV-related diseases. The use of a validated questionnaire and a comprehensive assessment of sociodemographic factors enhance the reliability and interpretability of the findings. However, several important limitations warrant consideration. The cross-sectional design precludes causal inferences about factors influencing HPV knowledge. Unicentric and the use of convenience sampling limit generalizability. 5. Conclusion Educational attainment emerged as the strongest predictor of HPV knowledge. Women with higher educational degrees scored 13-16% higher than those with a basic education. This underscores education's critical role in health literacy. These findings have immediate clinical implications for Iranian healthcare providers. 6. Declarations Acknowledgments The authors would like to thank all women who participated in the study. abstract_zh: 背景和目标:宫颈癌 是全球主要的公共卫生问题。本研究的目的是评估在三级妇科诊所就诊的女性对 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 和 宫颈癌 的态度和知识。材料和方法:这项描述性横断面调查对 2023 年至 2024 年德黑兰医科大学附属亚斯综合医院妇科诊所转诊的 139 名女性进行。数据收集通过面对面采访。使用 SPSS(IBM SPSS Statistics for Windows,版本 25)进行数据分析。P<0.05 被认为具有统计学显着性。结果:平均总知识得分为 25.07±5.92,满分为 33 分。参与者表现出很强的基础意识,正确地将 HPV 识别为性传播感染,认识到 HPV 影响两性,并认识到其在导致 宫颈癌 中的作用。然而,对垂直 传播 风险的了解以及缺乏针对 HPV 的特定 抗病毒药物 治疗 的知识很少。教育程度与知识水平显着相关(P=0.01)。事实上,教育程度是知识得分的最强预测因素。结论:在这种临床环境中,女性对 HPV 的基本认知度较高。然而,对于 治疗 选项、垂直 传播 和 疫苗接种 功效仍然存在严重误解。这些发现凸显了针对这些知识差距的教育干预措施的迫切需要,特别是在教育程度较低的女性中。他们还强调需要进行结构化的 HPV 教育和针对文化的宣传活动。

full_text: Abstract Background High-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) is a leading cause of anogenital cancers and disproportionately affects men who have sex with men (MSM), particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Few studies in sub-Saharan Africa have concurrently examined penile and rectal hrHPV infection and their site-specific behavioral and biological correlates. We assessed the prevalence, genotype distribution, and behavioral factors associated with penile and rectal hrHPV among MSM in Kisumu, Kenya. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from MSM aged 18–35 years. Clinician-collected penile and rectal swabs were tested for hrHPV using the ScreenFire HPV assay. Urine and rectal specimens were tested for Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae using GeneXpert, and HIV status was confirmed as per Kenyan national guidelines. hrHPV was analyzed separately by anatomical site. Log-binomial regression was used to estimate adjusted prevalence ratios (aPR) for associations with sociodemographic, behavioral, and biological factors. Results Penile hrHPV prevalence was 24.7% (39/158) and rectal hrHPV prevalence was 12.5% (22/176); 6.7% of participants tested at both sites had dual-site infection. Most infections at both sites involved a single genotype group. HPV-18/45 was the most common genotype group at both sites. Penile hrHPV was more likely among participants with HIV (aPR = 2.27, p = 0.050) and trended toward an association for those reporting insertive anal sex (aPR = 5.26, p = 0.062) and was less common among employed participants (aPR = 0.25, p = 0.048). Circumcision showed a protective trend (aPR = 0.52, p = 0.090). Rectal hrHPV was more common among participants with rectal chlamydia and/or gonorrhea infection (aPR = 3.34, p = 0.001), transgender or non-binary identity (aPR = 2.28, p = 0.036), with a possible association for those practicing receptive anal intercourse (aPR = 3.97, p = 0.062). Although HIV was associated with rectal hrHPV in unadjusted analyses, this relationship was attenuated after accounting for rectal bacterial STI infection. Conclusions hrHPV infection was common among MSM in Kisumu, Kenya, with distinct site-specific correlates. The strong association between rectal bacterial STIs and rectal hrHPV highlights the need for integrated HPV and STI screening. These findings support expansion of gender-neutral HPV vaccination and etiologic STI screening to reduce HPV-associated cancer risk among MSM in sub-Saharan Africa. title_original: Prevalence and behavioral factors associated with penile and rectal HPV infection among men who have sex with men in Kenya

analysis.research_question_and_background: High-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) is a leading cause of anogenital cancers and disproportionately affects men who have sex with men (MSM), particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Few studies in sub-Saharan Africa have concurrently examined penile and rectal hrHPV infection and their site-specific behavioral and biological correlates.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from MSM aged 18–35 years in Kisumu, Kenya. Clinician-collected penile and rectal swabs were tested for hrHPV using the ScreenFire HPV assay.
analysis.methods: Urine and rectal specimens were tested for Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae using GeneXpert, and HIV status was confirmed as per Kenyan national guidelines. Log-binomial regression was used to estimate adjusted prevalence ratios (aPR) for associations with sociodemographic, behavioral, and biological factors.
analysis.main_results: Penile hrHPV prevalence was 24.7% (39/158) and rectal hrHPV prevalence was 12.5% (22/176); 6.7% of participants tested at both sites had dual-site infection. HPV-18/45 was the most common genotype group at both sites. Penile hrHPV was more likely among participants with HIV (aPR = 2.27, p = 0.050) and less common among employed participants (aPR = 0.25, p = 0.048).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that hrHPV infection was common among MSM in Kisumu, Kenya, with distinct site-specific correlates. The strong association between rectal bacterial STIs and rectal hrHPV highlights the need for integrated HPV and STI screening.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support expansion of gender-neutral HPV vaccination and etiologic STI screening to reduce HPV-associated cancer risk among MSM in sub-Saharan Africa. Integrated screening could improve early detection and prevention of HPV-related diseases in this high-risk population.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was cross-sectional, limiting causal inference. The evidence strength is moderate due to the sample size and potential confounding factors, but the findings are consistent with biological plausibility and prior research.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the prevalence and behavioral factors associated with penile and rectal hrHPV infection among MSM in Kisumu, Kenya. A cross-sectional analysis of 158-176 participants aged 18-35 years found penile hrHPV prevalence at 24.7% and rectal hrHPV at 12.5%, with HPV-18/45 as the most common genotype. Key correlates included HIV status for penile infection and rectal bacterial STIs for rectal infection. The authors concluded that hrHPV is common with site-specific factors, supporting integrated HPV and STI screening and gender-neutral vaccination to reduce cancer risk in this population. The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, but the evidence strength is moderate.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 高风险 人乳头瘤病毒 (hrHPV) 是肛门生殖器癌症的主要原因,对男男性行为者 (MSM) 的影响尤为严重,特别是在低收入和中等收入国家。撒哈拉以南非洲地区很少有研究同时检查阴茎和直肠 hrHPV 感染及其特定部位的行为和生物学相关性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们对肯尼亚基苏木 18-35 岁 MSM 的基线数据进行了横断面分析。使用 ScreenFire HPV 检测对临床医生收集的阴茎和直肠拭子进行 hrHPV 检测。
elements_zh.methods: 使用 GeneXpert 对尿液和直肠标本进行沙眼衣原体和淋病奈瑟菌检测,并根据肯尼亚国家指南确认艾滋病毒状况。使用对数二项式回归来估计调整后的 患病率 比率 (aPR),以了解与社会人口统计学、行为和生物因素的关联。
elements_zh.main_results: 阴茎 hrHPV 患病率 为 24.7% (39/158),直肠 hrHPV 患病率 为 12.5% (22/176);在两个站点进行测试的参与者中有 6.7% 患有双站点感染。HPV-18/45 是两个地点最常见的基因型组。阴茎 hrHPV 在 HIV 感染者中更常见(aPR = 2.27,p = 0.050),而在就业参与者中则不太常见(aPR = 0.25,p = 0.048)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,hrHPV 感染在肯尼亚基苏木的 MSM 中很常见,并且具有明显的位点特异性相关性。直肠细菌性 STI 与直肠 hrHPV 之间的密切关联凸显了 HPV 和 STI 综合筛查的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持扩大性别中性 HPV 疫苗接种 和病因性 STI 筛查,以降低撒哈拉以南非洲 MSM 中 HPV 相关癌症风险。综合筛查可以改善这一高危人群中 HPV 相关疾病的早期发现和预防。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是横断面的,限制了因果推断。由于样本量和潜在的混杂因素,证据强度中等,但研究结果与生物学合理性和先前的研究一致。

full_text: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is responsible for almost 5% of cancers worldwide and drives malignancy by the sustained expression of the E6 and E7 viral oncoproteins. Despite its compact genome (~8 kb) encoding only eight proteins, HPV achieves substantial transcriptional complexity through extensive alternative RNA processing, a feature linked to the oncogenicity of high-risk HPV types such as HPV16. Historically, E7 expression was thought to originate exclusively from linear, alternatively processed transcripts. However, Zhao et al. challenged this view by identifying a circular RNA (circRNA) derived from high-risk HPV that retains the complete E7 gene capable of translating the E7 oncoprotein. These findings provide compelling evidence that viral circRNAs can actively contribute to cell transformation, mainly focusing on circE7 functions from HPV16. title: Case report: Penile collision tumor comprising HPV-associated squamous cell carcinoma and malignant melanoma
abstract: Collision tumors with squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) and malignant melanoma components are extremely rare. We report a case of a penile collision tumor with a component of HPV-associated SCC and malignant melanoma in a 61 year-old man. The patient underwent a partial penectomy and bilateral inguinal sentinel lymph node surgery. Microscopy showed a biphasic tumor with a component of SCC with warty-basaloid morphology, positive for HPV16 and 43, and a malignant melanoma associated with a BRAF mutation. This case posed diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to the absence of a precise TNM classification and documented treatment guidelines for this tumor type.

full_text: Abstract High-grade polymorphous adenocarcinoma (HG-PAC) is an exceptionally rare salivary gland malignancy, with very few cases reported in the sinonasal tract. A 74-year-old man presented with recurrence of a sinonasal tumor initially diagnosed as keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma. At recurrence, pathology showed a highly atypical, mitotically active neoplasm with solid growth and focal necrosis. Immunohistochemistry was positive for CK5, CK7, CK8/18, CD117, p16, p40, p63, and BCL2, with a Ki67 of 70%. Molecular testing excluded MYB rearrangement, common oncogenic variants (BRAF, EGFR, c-KIT, KRAS, PIK3CA), and high-risk HPV, supporting a diagnosis of HG-PAC. The patient underwent endoscopic-assisted resection followed by adjuvant radiotherapy and remains disease-free after 48 months. Literature confirms the rarity and diagnostic challenges of sinonasal HG-PAC and highlights the value of comprehensive pathological and molecular assessment. Despite aggressive features, long-term control is achievable with complete surgery and radiotherapy. This case adds to the limited evidence and supports multidisciplinary management. full_text_sections.full_text: Abstract High-grade polymorphous adenocarcinoma (HG-PAC) is an exceptionally rare salivary gland malignancy, with very few cases reported in the sinonasal tract. A 74-year-old man presented with recurrence of a sinonasal tumor initially diagnosed as keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma. At recurrence, pathology showed a highly atypical, mitotically active neoplasm with solid growth and focal necrosis. Immunohistochemistry was positive for CK5, CK7, CK8/18, CD117, p16, p40, p63, and BCL2, with a Ki67 of 70%. Molecular testing excluded MYB rearrangement, common oncogenic variants (BRAF, EGFR, c-KIT, KRAS, PIK3CA), and high-risk HPV, supporting a diagnosis of HG-PAC. The patient underwent endoscopic-assisted resection followed by adjuvant radiotherapy and remains disease-free after 48 months. Literature confirms the rarity and diagnostic challenges of sinonasal HG-PAC and highlights the value of comprehensive pathological and molecular assessment. Despite aggressive features, long-term control is achievable with complete surgery and radiotherapy. This case adds to the limited evidence and supports multidisciplinary management.
